item.title: 'I'm doing my best' - Allen thanks fans amid mental health struggles
item.description: Mark Allen has told fans that he is "doing his best to turn things around" and that he can "see the light" having spent the last 10 weeks in a mental health clinic, after saying he was in a "bad place" in an interview on Tuesday.

item.title: PSG's Kvaratskhelia set for surgery after ACL rupture in win over Barca

item.title: Flood submerges 18 Nasarawa communities, kills two
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has urged residents of flood-prone communities to heed warnings to relocate from low-lying areas to higher ground to avoid being swept away by recurring floods. The Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr Nawani Aboki, made the appeal on Monday while briefing journalists on the recent flooding that submerged 18 communities in a development area of Doma Local Government Area of the state. Aboki said two people had died in the disaster, while several residents had been displaced and buildings and farmlands destroyed. He said Governor Abdullahi Sule had directed the Director-General of the Nasarawa State Emergency Management Agency (NASEMA) to visit the affected communities to assess the extent of the damage and identify the necessary interventions. The commissioner said the government was expected to take concrete action following the assessment. “We are hoping that anytime this week, concrete actions will be taken by the government. Yesterday, when I was returning, I was there with the chairman of the local government to sympathise with the people and also condole with them,” he said. Describing the incident as massive flooding, Aboki expressed hope that the water would recede to allow residents to resume their normal activities. “It is not just normal flooding, but massive flooding that took place. We are hoping that the flooding will end and the waters will dry up so that people can resume their normal activities,” he said. He, however, warned residents against returning to their homes until the floodwaters had receded, citing concerns about the possibility of additional water flowing from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon. “But we have asked them not to go back yet. Let them wait until we see the water actually receding back to the River Benue again. We are not sure if more water will be coming in from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon. It will even be worse than it is currently,” he added. Aboki also reiterated the government’s commitment to providing support and relief supplies to the affected communities to prevent possible disease outbreaks. He explained that several smaller communities were clustered around larger settlements in the affected areas, increasing the pressure on host communities as displaced residents sought shelter. The commissioner cited Agyma, where more than eight communities were reportedly staying within the larger settlement, and Rukubi and Akpanaja, where several communities were also clustered. The government said it would continue to assess the situation and determine the necessary interventions as residents await the recession of the floodwaters. The post Flood submerges 18 Nasarawa communities, kills two appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: HCPAN to FG, States: Expand health insurance, review providers’ tarriffs
item.description: … Says 70% of healthcare spending comes from patients’ pockets … Only 10–13% of Nigerians covered by insurance … Seeks flexible premiums, prompt claims settlement By Chioma Obinna The HealthCare Providers Association of Nigeria (HCPAN), Lagos Branch, has called on the Federal and state governments to expand health insurance coverage, review tariffs paid to healthcare providers and ensure prompt settlement of claims, warning that low insurance penetration continues to expose millions of Nigerians to crippling medical expenses. The association said only about 10 to 13 per cent of Nigerians were covered by health insurance, while out-of-pocket payments accounted for approximately 70 per cent of healthcare expenditure, leaving many households financially vulnerable whenever illness occurs. HCPAN also called for flexible premium arrangements and community-based insurance schemes to bring market traders, artisans, transport workers, micro-entrepreneurs and other informal-sector workers into the health insurance system. item.dc:creator: Urowayino Jeremiah
item.content:encoded: … Says 70% of healthcare spending comes from patients’ pockets … Only 10–13% of Nigerians covered by insurance … Seeks flexible premiums, prompt claims settlement By Chioma Obinna The HealthCare Providers Association of Nigeria (HCPAN), Lagos Branch, has called on the Federal and state governments to expand health insurance coverage, review tariffs paid to healthcare providers and ensure prompt settlement of claims, warning that low insurance penetration continues to expose millions of Nigerians to crippling medical expenses. The association said only about 10 to 13 per cent of Nigerians were covered by health insurance, while out-of-pocket payments accounted for approximately 70 per cent of healthcare expenditure, leaving many households financially vulnerable whenever illness occurs. HCPAN also called for flexible premium arrangements and community-based insurance schemes to bring market traders, artisans, transport workers, micro-entrepreneurs and other informal-sector workers into the health insurance system. The association made the call at its Scientific Conference and Annual General Meeting, AGM, held in Lagos, with the theme, “Expanding Health Insurance Coverage in Nigeria: Improving Community-Based Insurance Schemes in the Informal Sector.” Speaking at the event, the Chairman of HCPAN Lagos Branch, Pharmacist Biola Paul-Ozieh, said the country’s high dependence on direct payments for healthcare remained a major obstacle to achieving universal health coverage, despite the mandatory health insurance provisions of the National Health Insurance Authority, NHIA, Act, 2022. “Currently, it is reported that about 10 to 13 per cent of the Nigerian population is covered by health insurance. The out-of-pocket expenditure is still huge at roughly 70 per cent despite the mandatory clause in the NHIA Act 2022,” she said. Paul-Ozieh added that coverage of vulnerable groups stood at about 3.8 million, while participation among informal-sector workers remained limited, with enrolment concentrated mainly in Lagos and Abuja. She identified delayed claims payments, tariffs that failed to reflect prevailing economic realities, negative attitudes among some enrollees and the exclusion of certain healthcare professionals from insurance programmes as challenges undermining providers’ participation. “The other concern we have as providers is the various challenges faced by varied professionals in not being included in the provision of health services in the health insurance programme,” she said. The HCPAN chairman said sustainable community-based insurance schemes would require stronger collaboration between government and private healthcare providers, alongside policies that addressed the financial realities of informal-sector workers. Informal sector holds key to wider coverage The Chief Executive Officer of DrugStoc Limited, Dr Chibuzo Opara, who delivered the keynote address through his representative, Dr Damilare Ojo, said expanding enrolment alone would not guarantee universal health coverage unless insurance schemes enabled beneficiaries to obtain the treatment and medicines they needed. “What does it mean to have health insurance if, when illness occurs, the person cannot access the care needed?” he asked. Opara said insurance coverage remained concentrated in the formal sector, leaving traders, artisans, transport workers and small-business owners inadequately protected against healthcare costs. He explained that irregular incomes made fixed insurance contributions difficult for many informal-sector workers, stressing that schemes must be designed around their economic circumstances. “We cannot close this gap by simply increasing enrolment in existing schemes. If we genuinely want to achieve universal health coverage, we must develop insurance models that address the needs of the people we intend to cover,” he said. He advocated flexible contributions, appropriate benefit packages and group enrolment through trusted associations to encourage participation. Opara also called for community pharmacies to be integrated into insurance networks, describing them as accessible points where residents could obtain initial healthcare advice and medicines. He urged stakeholders to assess the effectiveness of insurance schemes through measurable outcomes, including access to medicines, service utilisation, referral outcomes, claims processing times, policy renewals and reductions in out-of-pocket expenditure. Lagos expands grassroots enrolment Meanwhile, the Lagos State Government has reaffirmed its commitment to expanding health insurance through affordable premiums, grassroots enrolment and the integration of community pharmacies and diagnostic centres into the healthcare network. The state Commissioner for Health, Professor Akin Abayomi, represented by the Deputy Director of the Research Unit at the Lagos State Ministry of Health, Dr Tolu Babatope, said the informal sector accounted for a significant proportion of Lagos residents who often struggled to pay for medical treatment. He said the Lagos State Health Management Agency, LASHMA, was expanding affordable premium options and grassroots enrolment initiatives in line with the state’s policy on mandatory health insurance. Abayomi described community pharmacies as important entry points into the healthcare system, noting that their integration into insurance schemes could bring services closer to residents and strengthen access to treatment. “Community pharmacies, therefore, are no longer merely places where medicines are dispensed. They can serve as important points of contact for healthcare services and entry points into the health insurance network,” he said. He disclosed that the state was also working to strengthen links between pharmacies, hospitals and diagnostic centres, while addressing concerns about tariffs, delayed claims payments and inadequate digital infrastructure. Delivering the sub-theme, the Lagos Zonal Coordinator of the National Health Insurance Authority (NHIA), Pharmacist Femi Adeoye, who was represented by the State Coordinator, NHIA, Yaba Office, Pharmacist Chinenye Nwaohiri, highlighted opportunities for different healthcare professionals to participate in expanding health insurance. Adeoye said the NHIA operated programmes covering formal-sector workers, informal groups, private-sector participants and state health insurance schemes, with health maintenance organisations also supporting service delivery. He explained that initiatives such as the Basic Health Care Provision Fund and the Vulnerable Group Fund were designed to improve access to healthcare for people who might otherwise struggle to afford treatment. He called for fair tariff reviews that reflected the cost of providing services and urged healthcare professionals to take advantage of opportunities within the insurance system. “Fair tariff reviews and timely payment for services are essential to encouraging healthcare providers to participate in health insurance schemes and ensuring sustainable service delivery.” He stressed that public confidence depended on enrollees receiving timely and appropriate care, adding that reliable service delivery was essential to sustaining participation in insurance schemes. In his goodwill message, the National President of HCPAN, Dr Austin Aipoh, called for stronger collaboration among stakeholders and flexible payment arrangements to make health insurance more accessible to informal-sector workers. Aipoh said community-based approaches could help reach people whose incomes were irregular and who might not be able to afford conventional insurance contributions. He also urged policymakers to create an enabling environment for healthcare providers, stressing that insurance schemes must be structured to support both patients and the professionals responsible for delivering care. item.title: Java crashes the departure board at Tyne and Wear Metro
item.description: Java has elbowed its way onto a Tyne and Wear Metro information display, giving passengers an error message alongside their train times. Eagle-eyed Register reader abend0c4 spotted the sign, whose dialog design suggests a rather elderly Windows installation. Could it be Windows 7 in Classic guise, or perhaps Windows Server 2008 R2? Both wheezed their last in 2023, when the Extended Security Updates (ESU) program ended. Or perhaps POSReady 7? That kept going (again via ESU) until October 8, 2024 . Not that the end of ESU means the code will suddenly stop working. Just that Microsoft has called a halt to updates. The Tyne and Wear Metro is no stranger to keeping old technology running past its expiration date. Opened in August 1980 , the transit network has been replacing its aging rolling stock with new units, but the signage has endured. Then again, compared to the Commodore VIC-20 and Apple II, which ruled the home computing roost in 1980, perhaps an operating system that's only been obsolete for a few years isn't such a bad thing. Any second now somebody will be writing an email about some hardware by Sinclair, Acorn, or their particular device maker of choice. But back to the sign. Sadly, it's unclear which version of Java has elbowed its way to the foreground. Java's troubleshooting guidance lists video driver problems as one possible cause of this error. The train indicator seems to be operating as normal if somewhat obscured by Java's attempt to be the centre of attention," our reader noted. Java is longer be a bright young thing, yet it still keeps plenty of enterprise systems running behind the scenes. On this occasion, it appears to prefer the foreground. We'd prefer it kept a lower profile. Passengers have enough ups and downs without Java throwing its toys out of the virtual pram. ®

item.title: Jackson grad Abigail LaPole takes next step toward Team USA
item.description: A Stark County native is one of several athletes with the chance to participate in the International Wheelchair Basketball Federation Women's U25 Wheelchair Basketball World Championship. The National Wheelchair Basketball Association and the U25 Team Selection Committee picked Jackson High School graduate Abigail LaPole for their initial 20-player roster. LaPole, a freshman at the University of Texas-Arlington, previously played for the NWBA Junior Division's ASO Cavaliers and earned Varsity Invitational Tournament MVP honors in 2025. She is one of three UTA basketball players to make the roster. "Quinn (Meyer), Abby and Caroline (Fitzpatrick) making the initial roster is a testament to the hard work and dedication that they give to the sport of wheelchair basketball," UTA head women's wheelchair basketball coach John McPhail said in a UTA news release. "I'm excited to see them continue to develop and build on this opportunity throughout the rest of the semester and into the final selection camp in December. I know they will leave no stone unturned in pursuit of their goal of representing Team USA." LaPole has made headlines before as a star athlete at Jackson, winning three OHSAA state championships in seated shot put. Her senior year, she led the Polar Bears' wheelchair basketball team in scoring, averaging 16 points a game. The team lost in the 2025 state championship game to the Tallmadge Blue Devils. She was selected to the initial Team USA roster after participating in a tryout camp on Oct. 15–19 at the Lakeshore Foundation in Birmingham, Alabama. The 20 athletes will be invited to the selection camp from Dec. 13-17 at the U.S. Olympic & Paralympic Training Center in Colorado Springs. That group will be cut down to 12 for the 2027 U.S. Women’s U25 Wheelchair Basketball Team. The 12 will compete in the IWBF championships from June 11–17, 2027, in São Paulo, Brazil. The championships are held every four years; the United States won the last competition in 2023. Reach Aaron at 330-580-8428 or ahhughes@usatodayco.com. On X: @AaronHughe2 This article originally appeared on The Repository: Jackson grad Abigail LaPole takes next step toward Team USA

item.title: AFENIFERE RIFT: Those still making noise in cuckoo land – Omololu
item.description: By Dickson Omobola National Organising Secretary of Afenifere, Abagun Omololu, has expressed optimism about the future of the pan-Yoruba socio-cultural organisation after the death of its leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, saying those still making noise on the sidelines are crying in a cloud of cuckoo land. Recall that in the build-up to the 2023 general elections, which brought President Bola Tinubu to power, acting leader of Afenifere, the late Pa Ayo Adebanjo, supported Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, while the substantive leader, Fasoranti, supported Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, causing a division within the organisation. Speaking on The Morning Show, an Arise TV programme, Wednesday, Omololu described the period as unfortunate, saying such a development had never occurred in Yorubaland. He said: “It is an unfortunate period that we had before the 2023 election that got the acting leader and the substantive leader backing separate candidates. It’s an unfortunate thing. It had never happened in the history of Yorubaland.” On the future of Afenifere, he said: “The future of Afenifere is fantastic. Somebody came to be appointed a leader. The era of Baba Adebanjo is gone. Whoever that is still making noise on the side, I see it as a cry in a cloud of cuckoo land.” On Fasoranti’s legacy, he said: “To those of us who are very close to Baba, we have lost something in humanity. An embodiment of contentment, of somebody who sees public service as a sacrifice. Baba graduated from the University of Ibadan in 1951. There were not many graduates then. Immediately, he became a part of the Action Group of the late Obafemi Awolowo. He was a young man of 25 years old. Not many of his contemporaries were graduates. “Baba (Awolowo) pulled him, he worked with the likes of Professor Aluko, Professor Aboyade Cole and the rest. These are phenomenal leaders who came to the world for service. That is what Baba is for us. There was a time Baba lost his wife. Now he used to be made the governor of Ondo State, which a lot of people are dying for. They are using drug money, they are using everything now to buy the position. “The position was presented on the platter of gold to Baba, but he said, no, I cannot be a governor without having a wife, and I’m not ready to marry again. What a human being. Baba refused the position. That is why the position went to Baba Adefarati. This is a kind of human being. Baba’s life was Awoism. It’s not something where you march to gain political attention. It’s an inborn thing in him. We are going to serve the less privileged. That is what Baba is all about and Awoism. Egalitarian society. Let the rich get richer, while the poor must be looked after. These fingers are not equal. That is why they call us welfarists. That’s what Baba stood for. All his life. That was what Awolowo handed over to us.” The post AFENIFERE RIFT: Those still making noise in cuckoo land – Omololu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Glamorgan sign bowling all-rounder Mike
item.description: Ben Mike took 4 for 38 in Leicestershire's game against Glamorgan in August [Getty Images] Glamorgan have signed fast bowling all-rounder Ben Mike from Leicestershire. Nottingham-born Mike, 28, came through the Leicestershire academy and made his county debut for the Foxes in 2018. He has also had a spell with Yorkshire as well as playing on loan for Warwickshire. Mike, Glamorgan's first incoming signing for the 2027 season, has 125 first-class wickets to his name at an average of 37, and a top score of 99 not out. "I'm really excited to be joining Glamorgan and starting this new chapter in my career," Mike said. "Looking from the outside and from my first conversations with the club and Wally (director of cricket Mark Wallace), Glamorgan is clearly in an exciting place. "It's a club with a proud history but the recent achievements, ambition and direction of the club is very exciting." Glamorgan hunt coach again as Dawson joins England The numbers behind Glamorgan's rollercoaster survival

item.title: Mooresville Spinners reach lease resolution for renovated ballpark
item.description: The Mooresville Spinners will play in the town’s multimillion-dollar renovated baseball stadium now that the league has settled a lease dispute with the town. In July, the team told The Charlotte Observer the town wouldn’t let the league play there. The town said the team didn’t share a proposal like other leagues. However, in a joint statement, the two said they reached a mutual resolution regarding the park’s lease. “We are grateful to the Spinners fans and to this community for more than a decade of support, and we appreciate the support the Town of Mooresville extended to the Spinners over the years,” the team’s principal owner, John Wilcox, said in a release. “We are proud of the Spinners’ history at Moor Park, and we give credit to the Town for making that possible with its contributions.” The Town of Mooresville started on the stadium’s large-scale renovation in early 2025. It is set to open next year.

In July, the team told The Charlotte Observer the town wouldn’t let the league play there. The town said the team didn’t share a proposal like other leagues. However, in a joint statement, the two said they reached a mutual resolution regarding the park’s lease. “We are grateful to the Spinners fans and to this community for more than a decade of support, and we appreciate the support the Town of Mooresville extended to the Spinners over the years,” the team’s principal owner, John Wilcox, said in a release. “We are proud of the Spinners’ history at Moor Park, and we give credit to the Town for making that possible with its contributions.” The Town of Mooresville started on the stadium’s large-scale renovation in early 2025. It is set to open next year.

item.title: Barcelona report PSG to Uefa over ‘chainsaw massacre’ banner
item.description: Barcelona have reported Paris Saint-Germain to Uefa after supporters of the French side unveiled a banner displaying a masked man wielding a bloody chainsaw through their opponent’s club crest. The Halloween-themed tifo also carried the phase ‘Massacre, Parisian style’ and was displayed before PSG defeated Barcelona 4-2 at the Parc des Princes in the Champions League on Tuesday night. The tifo depicted a PSG supporter destroying the Barcelona badge with a chainsaw (UEFA via Getty Images) The PSG supporters also let off fireworks, creating sparks in the stands as the masked man cut through the Barcelona badge with his chainsaw, which could lead to a punishment from Uefa following an investigation of the match. The Press Association reported that Barcelona have now lodged a complaint to Uefa over the tifo, while ESPN reported that the Catalan believe the display was both “overly aggressive and offensive”. Uefa declined to comment, but its disciplinary body will usually assess reports from the game before deciding on any potential next steps or punishments. Barcelona suffered their first defeat of the season as they lost to the back-to-back European champions, with late goals from Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz earned the French side victory after Lamine Yamal had equalised. Meanwhile, PSG have confirmed that star winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has ruptured the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee , while Ousmane Dembele and captain Marquinhos are likely to miss the next several weeks due to thigh injuries suffered in the same match.

item.title: David Raya hopeful injured Bayern Munich ‘legend’ is fit to face Arsenal
item.description: David Raya hopeful injured Bayern Munich ‘legend’ is fit to face Arsenal Neuer remains a doubt for the Allianz Arena meeting after missing Bayern’s past two matches, but Raya would welcome the chance to face one of his childhood role models again. Photo by Shaun Botterill/Getty Images David Raya hopes Manuel Neuer is fit enough to face Arsenal tonight, with the goalkeeper describing the Bayern Munich captain as a “legend” and one of the players he admired growing up. Neuer remains a doubt for the Champions League meeting at the Allianz Arena after a foot problem kept him out of Bayern’s previous two matches. Rather than welcome the possible absence of one of the opposition’s most accomplished players, Raya made clear that he would relish another opportunity to share a pitch with him. Asked what he particularly admired about Neuer’s game, Raya said : “I like every single thing about Manuel Neuer. He’s a legend of the game, even though he’s still playing. What he’s done and what he has achieved, personally and collectively, is remarkable.” He continued: “He’s been a great goalkeeper and a great role model for a lot of young goalkeepers. When I was young, he was playing and I looked up to him. It’s just a pleasure to be sharing the pitch with him once again. Hopefully, he’s fit enough to play tomorrow.” Photo by Alex Grimm/Getty Images Raya did not single out one particular element of Neuer’s game. Elsewhere in his press conference, however, the Arsenal goalkeeper discussed his own enjoyment of playing with the ball at his feet and the challenge posed by Bayern’s aggressive press. “We know they press very high,” he said. “They go man to man,” Raya said, explaining that Arsenal hope to play through that pressure to create opportunities of their own. Whether Neuer will be involved remains uncertain. Bayern have described his problem as an accumulation of fluid on his foot, with sporting director Max Eberl playing down the seriousness of the issue after Saturday’s 6-1 victory over RB Leipzig . “It’s nothing serious – it’s just a bit of fluid on the foot,” he said. The problem was nevertheless been enough to rule the 40-year-old out of Bayern’s past two matches, the 3-3 Champions League draw away to Viking Stavanger and the emphatic Bundesliga win against Leipzig . Jonas Urbig deputised in both matches with Neuer training separately following the development of the problem before the trip to Norway. Eberl said Neuer was not ready to face Leipzig and that Bayern would assess whether he could return against Arsenal. As of Tuesday morning, he remains a doubt rather than a confirmed absentee. Photo by Richard Heathcote/Getty Images

item.title: Simone Inzaghi to Juventus? Former Inter boss emerges as SHOCK candidate to replace under-fire Luciano Spalletti
item.description: Al Hilal v Al Gharafa - AFC Champions League Elite - Getty Images Sport Luciano Spalletti is feeling the heat at Juventus following a sluggish start to the new Serie A campaign. Recent reports indicate that former Inter coach Simone Inzaghi has emerged as the top candidate to replace him. Pressure grows in Turin Spalletti is facing intense scrutiny at Juventus following a disappointing opening to the current season. The Italian manager has overseen a slow start, collecting just 11 points from his opening seven Serie A fixtures. With three wins, two draws, and two defeats, the Bianconeri are already off the pace. The club's leadership expected a far stronger launch, making Spalletti's position at the Allianz Stadium increasingly precarious. Despite the difficult run, club directors and ownership remain reluctant to sack the Tuscan tactician mid-season. Spalletti signed a long-term contract at the club that runs until 2028. Emergency backup plans While the board prefers patience, their stance will inevitably shift if domestic results fail to improve over the coming months. A continued slump would force club executives to appoint an interim manager to steady the ship. Stefano Pioli and Antonio Conte have both emerged as potential caretaker options should an immediate mid-season change become necessary. Both experienced Italian managers possess proven records at the highest level of Italian football. However, if Spalletti remains in charge until May but misses out on Champions League qualification, the hierarchy will seek a permanent replacement. Missing out on Europe's top competition represents a complete failure of their minimum seasonal target. Al Hilal v Al Fayha: Saudi Pro League Inzaghi top of wishlist Should Juventus seek a fresh long-term appointment, current Al-Hilal head coach Inzaghi is high on their shortlist, as per Gazzetta . The former Inter manager is heavily admired by senior decision-makers in Turin. Inzaghi boasts an incredible track record in Serie A, having guided Inter to the league title in the 2023-24 campaign. He also lifted two Coppa Italia trophies and three Supercoppa Italiana titles during his successful spell in Milan. Furthermore, the tactician proved his credentials on the continental stage by taking Inter to two Champions League finals in 2023 and 2025. His elite experience, player development skills, and tactical awareness make him an attractive long-term target. Crucial months ahead The immediate future rests entirely on Spalletti's ability to orchestrate a swift turnaround on the pitch. Juventus must embark on a consistent winning run to keep their league objectives alive and relieve executive pressure. If the current coaching team fails to secure top-four placement, a major managerial transition will take place. Inzaghi could then make a sensational return to Italian football ahead of the 2027-28 campaign. item.title: ‘Let’s Hope Everything Goes Well,’ ‘Let’s Hope Everyone Stays Safe’ — Ben Roethlisberger Weighs In as NFL Pushes Ahead With Steelers-Saints in Paris
item.description: ‘Let’s Hope Everything Goes Well,’ ‘Let’s Hope Everyone Stays Safe’ — Ben Roethlisberger Weighs In as NFL Pushes Ahead With Steelers-Saints in Paris Passports and phrasebooks were supposed to top the packing list for the NFL’s first-ever game in France, not security briefings. With violent unrest rattling Paris just days before Sunday’s Pittsburgh Steelers-New Orleans Saints game at Stade de France, Ben Roethlisberger weighed in as the league pushes ahead with its plans for a historic game in France. Ben Roethlisberger Chimes In on Steelers-Saints in Paris Steelers legend Ben Roethlisberger weighed in with a simple message on his “Footbahlin” podcast, looking ahead to Week 7: “Let’s hope everything goes well. Let’s hope everyone stays safe (and) everyone over there is safe.” His words come as the NFL stands firm on playing the game as scheduled, with kickoff set for 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday, Oct. 25. However, that stance has already drawn a pointed question from much closer to the Steelers’ locker room. Dani Watt, T.J. Watt’s wife and a former NWSL player, has more reason than most to keep tabs on the news out of France. Her husband and his teammates are due to travel to the French capital later this week for the Week 7 matchup in Saint-Denis. The Saints are already settled in, staying just outside the city center on the outskirts of Versailles, according to Fox. On Monday, Oct. 19, she shared a CBS Pittsburgh graphic to her Instagram Stories that read, “The NFL says it is continuing forward with plans for the upcoming Steelers-Saints game amid unrest in Paris.” Rather than let the graphic speak for itself, she chose to add a question of her own over the top: “Tell me how this one makes sense???” PICK THE PLAYOFF FIELD: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Both Teams and the NFL Stand by Their Security Plans Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy struck a different note that same day, saying at his press conference that he’s “obviously very aware” of the unrest before adding, “We feel like we have a really good plan, we’re aware of the situations over there and have a lot of confidence in our plan.” For its part, the league hasn’t budged an inch, saying in a statement on Sunday, Oct. 18, “We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There’s been no disruption or impact at league sites.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer The Saints are singing from the same hymn sheet, with executive Greg Bensel saying in a statement that same day, “We concur with the NFL’s statement and are planning to play the game. Members of our football operations staff and internal security team have been on the ground in France for the past few days, and there has been no disruption or impact at any of our team sites.” Peter O’Reilly, the NFL’s executive vice president of club business, international and league events, then doubled down in a brie
item.content:encoded: ‘Let’s Hope Everything Goes Well,’ ‘Let’s Hope Everyone Stays Safe’ — Ben Roethlisberger Weighs In as NFL Pushes Ahead With Steelers-Saints in Paris Passports and phrasebooks were supposed to top the packing list for the NFL’s first-ever game in France, not security briefings. With violent unrest rattling Paris just days before Sunday’s Pittsburgh Steelers-New Orleans Saints game at Stade de France, Ben Roethlisberger weighed in as the league pushes ahead with its plans for a historic game in France. Ben Roethlisberger Chimes In on Steelers-Saints in Paris Steelers legend Ben Roethlisberger weighed in with a simple message on his “Footbahlin” podcast, looking ahead to Week 7: “Let’s hope everything goes well. Let’s hope everyone stays safe (and) everyone over there is safe.” His words come as the NFL stands firm on playing the game as scheduled, with kickoff set for 9:30 a.m. ET on Sunday, Oct. 25. However, that stance has already drawn a pointed question from much closer to the Steelers’ locker room. Dani Watt, T.J. Watt’s wife and a former NWSL player, has more reason than most to keep tabs on the news out of France. Her husband and his teammates are due to travel to the French capital later this week for the Week 7 matchup in Saint-Denis. The Saints are already settled in, staying just outside the city center on the outskirts of Versailles, according to Fox. On Monday, Oct. 19, she shared a CBS Pittsburgh graphic to her Instagram Stories that read, “The NFL says it is continuing forward with plans for the upcoming Steelers-Saints game amid unrest in Paris.” Rather than let the graphic speak for itself, she chose to add a question of her own over the top: “Tell me how this one makes sense???” PICK THE PLAYOFF FIELD: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Both Teams and the NFL Stand by Their Security Plans Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy struck a different note that same day, saying at his press conference that he’s “obviously very aware” of the unrest before adding, “We feel like we have a really good plan, we’re aware of the situations over there and have a lot of confidence in our plan.” For its part, the league hasn’t budged an inch, saying in a statement on Sunday, Oct. 18, “We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There’s been no disruption or impact at league sites.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer The Saints are singing from the same hymn sheet, with executive Greg Bensel saying in a statement that same day, “We concur with the NFL’s statement and are planning to play the game. Members of our football operations staff and internal security team have been on the ground in France for the past few days, and there has been no disruption or impact at any of our team sites.” Peter O’Reilly, the NFL’s executive vice president of club business, international and league events, then doubled down in a briefing on Tuesday, saying that the league’s plans for the game in Paris this weekend “are moving forward as planned.” “We’ve got confidence in the plans, both from an ops and a security standpoint,” O’Reilly added. The unrest behind the concern has been building for weeks. It dates back to mid-September, when students and teachers at a school in the Paris suburbs walked out to demand more resources and staffing, before protests spread across the city over living costs, calls for more government action and the widening wealth gap. At least 1,800 people were taken into custody across France during last weekend’s protests as violent groups battled police, according to CBS Pittsburgh, and Paris police put the capital region’s share at 855 on Sunday. Subsequent reporting in France put the arrest total at approximately 2,400. Reports of looting and damage came from around Place de la République, roughly 5 miles south of Stade de France. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Tribe aims to help Jersey despite England ambitions
item.description: Asa Tribe's 175 not out against Papua New Guinea last year is the highest score made in an ICC Challenge League match [ICC] Asa Tribe says he is "absolutely delighted" to be returning to play for Jersey as the island team aims to keep their Cricket World Cup hopes alive. The Glamorgan and England Lions batter has not played for his homeland since the summer of 2025 after a remarkable rise in the English domestic game. But Tribe, 22, who made his international debut for Jersey as a 17-year-old five years ago, hopes he can help the island qualify from ICC Challenge League A after returning to their squad for the first time since last summer. Jersey top the six-team pool and need just two more wins to ensure they progress to the 2026 Cricket World Cup Qualifier Play-off in Nepal in December. "I've had a bit of a busy last 12 months and I'm happy to be playing for Jersey again," he told BBC Radio Jersey "The last couple of times that I was in a Jersey shirt were successful for myself and the team. "I really enjoy putting those kind of performances in for Jersey because I know what it means for the side in the sense of what it can go towards and how we can progress as a side." Tribe's last matches for Jersey came in the last round of fixtures in Challenge League A last summer - he scored 175 in a 160-run win over Papua New Guinea before hitting an unbeaten 53 in an eight-wicket win over Qatar. "That one is quite close to my heart," Tribe says of the 175 against Papua New Guinea, which is a record score for an individual batter in the ICC Challenge League. "That was one of the games where we needed someone to stand up, there was a bit going on with the ball, we were batting first on one that was doing a little bit and I feel that knock set that game up really nicely. " Tribe in Jersey team for World Cup Challenge final round Tribe hits third century of week in Jersey win Tribe's knock of 175 was his third List A century in the space of a week after scoring two for Glamorgan. That scoring set the foundations for his call-up to the England Lions squad that winter - a team he will tour with to the Caribbean next month. He has gone on to play franchise cricket in South Africa and Canada and with Welsh Fire in The Hundred, as well as become a key part of the Glamorgan side that kept their Division One status in the County Championship this year after winning promotion in 2025 following 20 years in the second tier. It has also led people to link Tribe with a call-up to the full England side. "It's a huge ambition of mine," he said. "I have had a small taste for it in the Lions stuff and I really want to make that stride to keep going and keep getting better and keep pushing for the next stage in my career, which I hope is England." "I really enjoy putting those kind of performances in for Jersey because I know what it means for the side in the sense of what it can go towards and how we can progress as a side." "That was one of the games where we needed someone to stand up, there was a bit going on with the ball, we were batting first on one that was doing a little bit and I feel that knock set that game up really nicely. " Tribe in Jersey team for World Cup Challenge final round Tribe hits third century of week in Jersey win Tribe's knock of 175 was his third List A century in the space of a week after scoring two for Glamorgan. That scoring set the foundations for his call-up to the England Lions squad that winter - a team he will tour with to the Caribbean next month. He has gone on to play franchise cricket in South Africa and Canada and with Welsh Fire in The Hundred, as well as become a key part of the Glamorgan side that kept their Division One status in the County Championship this year after winning promotion in 2025 following 20 years in the second tier. It has also led people to link Tribe with a call-up to the full England side. "It's a huge ambition of mine," he said. "I have had a small taste for it in the Lions stuff and I really want to make that stride to keep going and keep getting better and keep pushing for the next stage in my career, which I hope is England." He added: "The side's very strong so it's not something that I'm just going to walk into. "It does mean really being hard and cut-throat about where my game actually is. How good is it? How do I get better? What areas do I need to work on? What's going to give me the best chance to move up to that level? "If it's such a competitive environment then how, if I do get an opportunity, am I going to be ready to take it straight away? So what challenges will I face there? "That's something I'm constantly looking at and trying to find the balance between getting better whilst also nailing down my current strengths." Asa Tribe came up through Jersey's ranks before being spotted by Glamorgan while playing cricket at university in Cardiff [ICC] Tribe would not the be first player from an associate nation to be called up by England. The Durham batter was called up by England for their first Test against New Zealand in June. "I think the position we're in for this tournament is a really good one," he says. "Only really requiring to win two or three games is a position you'd love to be in rather than at the start of the tournament where you're thinking about needing to win every game. "I think this tournament should be really good for us. Hopefully we get the job done here and we can look ahead to December and really stake a claim for some ODI status and potentially some more World Cup fixtures."

item.title: Shaquille O’Neal says he will only create a Kobe Bryant documentary on one condition
item.description: Photo credit should read AFP/AFP via Getty Images Shaquille O’Neal has opened up about why he is not keen on making a documentary about his former teammate Kobe Bryant. The two former Los Angeles Lakers stars formed one of the most dominant and iconic duos in NBA history and won three championships in a row together. Since retirement, O’Neal has entered into several different ventures, and one of them is a production company. Is a Bryant documentary a potential future project? The answer is no. Shaquille O’Neal names his condition to create a Kobe Bryant documentary Bryant is always in the conversation when you are discussing the greatest basketball player of all time, and he is adored even to this day. O’Neal knows about his old teammate’s ability more than anyone else, and with a production house now under him, we’re sure fans would love an in-depth documentary. The hugely popular Allen Iv3rson docuseries on Prime was co-produced by O’Neal’s production company, Jersey Legends, and was highly acclaimed. But no such series or documentary about Bryant is planned or is in the works, claims the former Lakers number 34, and he isn’t going to work on one unless his old pal’s family asks him to do so. He told Variety: “I wouldn’t want to do one because that enigmatic, legendary story’s been told. If I was asked to do it by his family, then I would do it, but I’m not just going to do it to be doing it.” The respect O’Neal has for Bryant’s legacy, as well as his family, is very clear to see in his statement above, where he has categorically refused to capitalise on their storied history just for entertainment. That being said, should the Bryant family give their blessing and O’Neal agrees to create a docuseries, we’re convinced it would be a fantastic watch. Read more: ‘I was a Kobe Bryant guy’ – Carter Bryant reveals extreme Spurs offseason routine Bill Simmons makes interesting ‘1999 Kobe Bryant’ comparison for Dylan Harper Austin Reaves gives Kobe Bryant reason for wearing Nike shoes despite being a Rigorer athlete

item.title: Mac Allister reflects on ‘really difficult’ last year and praises Iraola’s impact
item.description: Mac Allister reflects on ‘really difficult’ last year and praises Iraola’s impact Alexis Mac Allister has admitted he was below his best last season but believes Andoni Iraola has helped change the mood and direction at Liverpool. The midfielder was candid about his own performances during the last campaign after Tuesday’s comeback win over Villarreal, in which he scored twice, saying he knew his level had dropped during a difficult year. “Last year was a really difficult year for all of us,” Mac Allister said. “It was clear that I was not at the level. I am the first one to say [that], I have no problem. “Something wasn’t right in the group. This manager changed it, and that’s really important.” Mac Allister also highlighted the difference in Liverpool’s approach under Iraola. “The way we play it is quite different,” he said. “I don’t like to compare. I’m feeling good right now, that’s what I want, and that’s what I enjoy. “From the first day we started working together, I saw something really important,” he said. “I think we are going in the right direction but if you look at the game today, it was far from perfect so we need to work, keep giving everything. “It’s a really important year for us so hopefully we can win some trophies.” The Argentina international also addressed his future, with no new deal yet offered by the club with the 27-year-old out of contract in 2028. “When I said what I said, it was more about my emotion and my feelings,” he said, when asked about his previous comments about being “sad” that a new deal had not been discussed . “That’s their decision and that’s completely fine to me. “I do what I always do, give my best in training, here in the games, and in the end we’ll see what happens.”

item.title: OU football faces Jeff Lebby, only OC hire Brent Venables got right | Mussatto's Minutes
item.description: NORMAN — Oklahoma’s offense under Brent Venables hasn’t always been an abomination. In fact, in his first two years as head coach, the offense did the heavy lifting as Venables worked to rebuild a shoddy defensive infrastructure. The Sooners went 6-7 in 2022, Venables’ first season, with an offense that ranked 13th and a defense that ranked 122nd. OU improved to 10-3 in 2023 behind the No. 3 offense in the country and a defense that ranked 79th. Those were the days when the Sooners had themselves a quarterback. Imagine this team with Dillon Gabriel in place of John Mateer. But the Sooners also had a big-time offensive coordinator in Jeff Lebby, whose two-year tenure in Norman was most certainly underappreciated. ( I thought Mississippi State did OU a favor by hiring him away , but that had everything to do with the Art Briles of it all and nothing to do with Lebby’s offensive acumen). Regardless of how anyone feels about Lebby, OU’s offense has been in a ditch ever since he left. OU football stock report: Sooners freshman DE Jake Kreul breaks out vs Kentucky When the Bulldogs host the Sooners on Saturday in Starkville, Mississippi, Venables will be coaching opposite the only offensive coordinator hire he got right. Seth Littrell didn’t last a full season in the job, and Ben Arbuckle is on the two-and-done track. The Sooners, by total offense, rank last among Power Four teams. Surprising it’s not worse. John Mateer has regressed, the offensive line is in shambles and the Sooners are short on playmakers. Just when Venables did the impossible by getting OU to play elite defense, the offense tanked. Lebby is 3-17 in the SEC since taking over in Starkville, but the Bulldogs are a tough out when healthy. Mississippi State was blanked by LSU last weekend, but the Bulldogs were without star quarterback Kamario Taylor and leading rusher Fluff Bothwell. Before the LSU game, the Bulldogs were averaging 487 yards per game — almost 7 yards per play — which would rank ninth nationally. Taylor, who’s become a phenom in Lebby’s offense, has a 17-to-4 touchdown/interception ratio. Mateer has thrown nine touchdowns and seven interceptions. “(Lebby) goes fast, and their offense is almost warp speed at times,” OU defensive tackles coach Todd Bates said Tuesday. Bates, who also holds the title of associate head coach, filled in for an under-the-weather Venables at OU’s weekly news conference. Bates and the Sooners know Lebby’s system, and vice versa. “Jeff’s going to have them ready to play,” Bates said. “We’ll be ready to play too.” More: Why did OU football leave OL Ryan Fodje in game despite injury? An ace move by Sam Presti and Co., who signed Wallace to a long-term extension Sunday night . Among 2023 draftees, Wallace ranks second in games, eighth in assists and 13th in points and rebounds.

Lebby is 3-17 in the SEC since taking over in Starkville, but the Bulldogs are a tough out when healthy. Mississippi State was blanked by LSU last weekend, but the Bulldogs were without star quarterback Kamario Taylor and leading rusher Fluff Bothwell. Before the LSU game, the Bulldogs were averaging 487 yards per game — almost 7 yards per play — which would rank ninth nationally. Taylor, who’s become a phenom in Lebby’s offense, has a 17-to-4 touchdown/interception ratio. Mateer has thrown nine touchdowns and seven interceptions. “(Lebby) goes fast, and their offense is almost warp speed at times,” OU defensive tackles coach Todd Bates said Tuesday. Bates, who also holds the title of associate head coach, filled in for an under-the-weather Venables at OU’s weekly news conference. Bates and the Sooners know Lebby’s system, and vice versa. “Jeff’s going to have them ready to play,” Bates said. “We’ll be ready to play too.” More: Why did OU football leave OL Ryan Fodje in game despite injury? Ben Arbuckle explains Where Cason Wallace would go in 2023 NBA redraft? The Thunder traded up in the 2023 NBA Draft to take Kentucky guard Cason Wallace with the No. 10 pick. An ace move by Sam Presti and Co., who signed Wallace to a long-term extension Sunday night . Among 2023 draftees, Wallace ranks second in games, eighth in assists and 13th in points and rebounds. He’s also No. 1 in steals. According to Basketball Reference’s VORP (value over replacement player) and win shares metrics, Wallace has been the third-most valuable player in the draft behind Victor Wembanyama and Amen Thompson. So, where would Wallace go if we were redrafting? I’m approaching this as if teams could go back in time to address their current needs. 1. Victor Wembanyama (Spurs): Solid pick by San Antonio. Actual pick: Victor Wembanyama 2. Brandon Miller (Hornets): Miller just signed a five-year, $209 million extension. Yet to turn 24, the do-it-all wing could be a mult-time All-Star. Actual pick: Brandon Miller 3. Amen Thompson (Trail Blazers): Scoot Henderson, whom the Blazers drafted here, could still turn into a good NBA player. But Thompson is already a very good NBA player. And if he ever learns how to shoot, he’s an All-NBA player. Actual pick: Scoot Henderson 4. Ausar Thompson (Rockets): The Rockets lose out on Amen, but they get the next best thing in Ausar — not as good as his brother offensively but maybe better defensively. You could make the case for Wallace here, but I don’t see the Rockets passing on a Thompson twin. The upside is crazy high. Actual pick: Amen Thompson 5. Keyonte George (Pistons): What if Detroit had drafted the anti-Ausar? That’s basically what Keyonte George is. He’s a minus defender, but he’s a big-time scorer who could take a big chunk of the offensive burden off Cade Cunningham. I love this hypothetical. Actual pick: Ausar Thompson NBA predictions: Why Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Thunder will win their second championship 6. Cason Wallace (Magic): Wallace doesn’t alleviate Orlando’s offensive woes, but he’s too much of a game-changing defender to fall lower than this. Wallace is a better version of what the Magic has in Jalen Suggs. Actual pick: Anthony Black 7. Toumani Camara (Wizards via Pacers): Camara, who went 52nd overall, is a big riser in the redraft. He’s a 6-foot-7 defensive terror and an improving 3-point shooter. The type of player every team needs. Actual pick: Bilal Coulibaly 8. Jaime Jaquez Jr. (Pacers via Wizards): This draft starts to thin out. But the Pacers get Jaquez, the reigning Sixth Man of the Year runner-up. Actual pick: Jarace Walker 9. Anthony Black (Jazz): Black and George could’ve been a fun backcourt pairing. I still really like Black’s overall game. Actual pick: Taylor Hendricks 10. Brandin Podziemski (Thunder via Mavericks): The Thunder traded up for Wallace, which turned out to be a great move. I don’t know if doing the same for Podziemski makes sense, but he’s a solid all-around guard. He just doesn’t have an elite carrying skill. Actual pick: Cason Wallace More: A complete guide on how to watch OKC Thunder in 2026-27 NBA season OU-Mississippi State set for first meeting Of the 68 Power Four teams, plus Notre Dame, OU has played all but five in football. One of which will be crossed off Saturday when OU plays at Mississippi State. The Bulldogs are the last remaining SEC team the Sooners have yet to face. Here are the other four Power Four programs the Sooners have yet to play. Georgia Tech: Georgia Tech is the only ACC team the Sooners haven’t played. OU is the only SEC team the Yellow Jackets haven’t played. Michigan State: The Spartans haven’t played an SEC team in the regular season since 1947, when they hosted both Kentucky and Mississippi State. Purdue: An Oklahoman, Barry Odom, coaches the Boilermakers. Rutgers: The Scarlet Knights have never played an Oklahoma team. Bedlam bets Here are my OU and OSU picks for the week. OU at Mississippi State Line: Sooners by 3.5 Pick: Sooners 23, Bulldogs 16 This is awfully difficult to pick without knowing the status of Mississippi State star quarterback Kamario Taylor (foot). Even if Taylor plays, you wouldn’t expect him to be 100% healthy. Having to face an elite defense in his return would be no remedy. OU’s offense versus Mississippi State’s defense is a battle of two of the worst units in the SEC. I think the Sooners can move the ball against the Bulldogs. On the flip side, Venables knows Jeff Lebby’s offense and Lebby knows Venables’ defense. OU by a touchdown. Picking the Sooners this season: 4-2 straight up, 4-2 against the spread OSU vs. Colorado Line: Cowboys by 13.5 Pick: Cowboys 35, Buffaloes 17 Colorado played Utah to a field goal last week in Boulder, but I don’t think the Buffaloes are much of a threat here. It’s homecoming for the Cowboys, and they’re going to be playing hungry after the loss at Houston. Colorado’s defense has held up OK, but the Buffs can’t move the ball. It’s a get-right opportunity for OSU’s defense. Picking the Cowboys this season: 4-2 straight up, 3-3 against the spread NFL Sooner of the Week Caleb Williams, QB, Bears: He was sharp in his first game back after missing a month with a hamstring injury. item.title: Off-Script Ohio: Sayin’s status, the quarterback battle and midseason grades
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, IN - OCTOBER 17: Luke Fahey (13) of the Ohio State Buckeyes turns to hand off to Isaiah West (32) during the college football game against the Indiana Hoosiers on October 17, 2026 at Memorial Stadium in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Joe Robbins/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The bye week news hasn’t been kind to Ohio State. Julian Sayin is now out indefinitely. He technically hasn’t been ruled out for the season, but my guess is we won’t see him again this year. With Sayin out, both Luke Fahey and Tavien St. Clair will get first-team reps over the next two weeks before Ohio State travels to USC. Injury news The two quarterbacks couldn’t be more different. St. Clair was a five-star recruit and the No. 3 quarterback in the 2025 class, and he’s listed at 6-foot-4 and 235 pounds. In limited action, he’s 5-of-7 for 52 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Fahey was a three-star and the No. 36 quarterback in the 2026 class, listed at 5-foot-11 and 206 pounds. He’s 9-of-11 for 203 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. Whoever wins it, the offense will have to lean on the run game and Jeremiah Smith. That run game took a hit too. Ja’Kobi Jackson needs surgery and will be out about a month. The hope is that he’s back for Michigan, which puts even more on Bo Jackson’s shoulders in the meantime. Midseason position grades Cole and Joey go position by position, comparing what was expected of each group heading into the season with how they’ve actually performed through the first half of the year. From the running backs and wide receivers to the defensive front and special teams, they evaluate which units have lived up to expectations, which have exceeded them, and which still have work to do.

item.title: Bayern Munich vs. Arsenal predicted XI: Bayern without Michael Olise and Joshua Kimmich
item.description: Bayern Munich vs. Arsenal predicted XI: Bayern without Michael Olise and Joshua Kimmich Due to a passing in his immediate family, Bayern Munich have confirmed that Joshua Kimmich will not be in the squad today for the UEFA Champions League match against Arsenal. In his place, Tom Bischof is expected to start alongside Aleksandar Pavlović. Manuel Neuer is also expected to return in goal in place of Jonas Urbig after missing their 6-1 victory over RB Leipzig on Saturday. Konrad Laimer, Dayot Upamecano and Kim Minjae are each expected to retain their place, but Alphonso Davies could be tasked with marking Bukayo Saka, in place of Nathaniel Brown. Bischof made his stamp on the German national team during the recent international break, and he is set to replace Kimmich at the heart of Bayern’s midfield. Additionally, Bayern will be without Michael Olise after his red card against Viking FK last week, which could see Lennart Karl starting in his place. Jamal Musiala is currently sidelined which saw Ismail Saibari start against Leipzig, but Serge Gnabry could be given the nod against his former club. Predicted Bayern Munich vs. Arsenal starting line-ups Bayern Munich: Neuer – Laimer, Upamecano, Kim, Davies – Bischof, Pavlovic – Karl, Gnabry, Luis Diaz – Kane Arsenal: Raya – Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Hincapie – Rice, Lewis-Skelly – Saka, Ødegaard, Madueke – Havertz GGFN | Daniel Pinder

item.title: Oilers’ Mike Babcock credits ‘ultra-competitive’ Devon Levi after OT win vs. Wild
item.description: Edmonton Oilers head coach Mike Babcock praised Devon Levi’s competitiveness after the goaltender helped secure a 4-3 overtime victory against the Minnesota Wild on Tuesday. Levi stopped 27 shots as Edmonton improved to 7-1-1 this NHL season. Evan Bouchard scored the overtime winner at 3:32, converting a power play after Minnesota received a too-many-men penalty. The victory also extended Edmonton’s strong run, with the team winning seven of its last eight games. MORE: Connor McDavid reacts as injury-hit Oilers fall to Utah Mammoth Babcock credited the Oilers’ penalty kill for its improved performance against Minnesota’s dangerous power play. However, he made sure to recognize Levi’s contribution between the pipes. “Now, let’s not take anything away from Levi. He made some good saves,” Babcock told reporters . He highlighted a second-chance stop in the third period, describing Levi’s right-pad save as “an unreal save.” Babcock then mentioned Wild goalie Jesper Wallstedt, who made 28 saves and said, “Now, their goaltender was spectacular. I mean, absolutely spectacular. So, good for him. And, they’re both good enough that if you don’t climb on them, you’re not going to score.” Mike Babcock highlights Devon Levi’s competitive mindset Edmonton Oilers head coach Mike Babcock watches game action. Mandatory Credit: Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Babcock also praised Levi’s attitude and work ethic when asked what stood out about the young goaltender’s makeup. “Well, I mean, he’s ultra-competitive,” Babcock said. “What I like about Levi, every day I walk in here, he’s got a smile on his face. He’s always working out. He’s always working.” The Oilers coach also pointed to Levi’s confidence and family background when explaining his positive impression. “He’s competitive as can be. Feels good about himself. When you meet his mom and dad, you see why,” Babcock added. “I mean, he just seems like a great kid.” Levi has made the most of his opportunity in Edmonton after arriving from Buffalo on July 1. His record now stands at 5-1-0, giving the Oilers valuable stability in goal. Babcock recognised his stats, saying, “I mean, not a bad record. So, good for him.” "It was a great win for our team, our specialty teams were outstanding. Coming in, we talked a ton about that, that it was gonna be a huge factor in the game & I thought they were fantastic." Coach Babcock on the #Oilers victory over Minnesota. @Enterprise | #LetsGoOilers pic.twitter.com/S5T9vfgZUP — Edmonton Oilers (@EdmontonOilers) October 21, 2026 MORE: Blue Jackets’ reunion with Kirill Marchenko comes with ‘feelings still raw’ Edmonton overcame Minnesota’s third-period comeback, which included goals from Kirill Kaprizov and Ryan Hartman. Bouchard’s power-play finish ultimately secured two points. Levi’s recent performances have strengthened his case for a larger role. item.title: The world’s first spinal cord transplant has been performed in Russia
item.description: A surgeon has told New Scientist they have performed a transplant on someone with a complete spinal cord injury using a piece of spinal cord from a brain-dead donor, but researchers have raised concerns

item.title: Phillies Get Update On Triple Crown MVP Free Agent Target
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA - DECEMBER 08: President of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski of the Philadelphia Phillies talks to the media during the introductory press conference for Trea Turner at Citizens Bank Park on December 8, 2022 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Getty Images The Philadelphia Phillies face another pivotal offseason after falling well short of their ultimate goal in the postseason. With questions surrounding the lineup’s long-term production, the front office could look overseas for the kind of impact bat capable of changing the team’s fortunes. Philadelphia has reason to consider making a significant investment in its offense, particularly as its veteran core ages. “The position player core was not good in 2026, and (Bryce) Harper and Kyle Schwarber, the two mainstays who carried this group, aren’t getting any younger, so this is an ever-growing concern,” David Schoenfield noted for ESPN . Now, the Phillies have received an important update on one potential solution they’ve been targeting. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets’ $17 Million Castoff Sends 5-Word Yankees Message Philadelphia Phillies Target Superstar Triple Crown Winner Heading For Free Agency On Monday, the Phillies received an update on Teruaki Sato, a Japanese slugger whose historic season has positioned him to pursue an MLB contract this winter. “One of the biggest dominoes of the impending MLB offseason has fallen, adding a massive free agent bat to a pool that is relatively light on them,” Max Ralph reported for MLB.com . “The Hanshin Tigers of Nippon Professional Baseball announced that they will approve the posting of superstar infielder Teruaki Sato to MLB this offseason.” Sato will enter the market after a remarkable campaign with the Tigers. He won the Central League Triple Crown by hitting .306 with 39 home runs and 106 RBIs, putting himself in position to pursue a second consecutive league MVP award. Ralph noted that the Phillies have been among the teams linked to Sato. And MLB insider Jon Heyman has also reported that the Phillies are targeting him. Most recently, Japanese media reported that the Phillies had representatives in Japan to watch Sato in person. “On the field, (Sato) led the team to its first-ever consecutive Central League championships and won the Triple Crown,” Yahoo! Japan noted in a translated report published last week . “On this day, scouts from the (Texas) Rangers, Phillies, and other American teams were also in attendance.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Dodgers Veteran Backstop Cuts Ties With Team Immediately After Season Ends Philadelphia Phillies Face Major Free Agency Decision After Teruaki Sato News Sato primarily plays third base, although he has also spent time in the outfield. item.content:encoded: PHILADELPHIA, PA - DECEMBER 08: President of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski of the Philadelphia Phillies talks to the media during the introductory press conference for Trea Turner at Citizens Bank Park on December 8, 2022 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Getty Images The Philadelphia Phillies face another pivotal offseason after falling well short of their ultimate goal in the postseason. With questions surrounding the lineup’s long-term production, the front office could look overseas for the kind of impact bat capable of changing the team’s fortunes. Philadelphia has reason to consider making a significant investment in its offense, particularly as its veteran core ages. “The position player core was not good in 2026, and (Bryce) Harper and Kyle Schwarber, the two mainstays who carried this group, aren’t getting any younger, so this is an ever-growing concern,” David Schoenfield noted for ESPN . Now, the Phillies have received an important update on one potential solution they’ve been targeting. FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Mets’ $17 Million Castoff Sends 5-Word Yankees Message Philadelphia Phillies Target Superstar Triple Crown Winner Heading For Free Agency On Monday, the Phillies received an update on Teruaki Sato, a Japanese slugger whose historic season has positioned him to pursue an MLB contract this winter. “One of the biggest dominoes of the impending MLB offseason has fallen, adding a massive free agent bat to a pool that is relatively light on them,” Max Ralph reported for MLB.com . “The Hanshin Tigers of Nippon Professional Baseball announced that they will approve the posting of superstar infielder Teruaki Sato to MLB this offseason.” Sato will enter the market after a remarkable campaign with the Tigers. He won the Central League Triple Crown by hitting .306 with 39 home runs and 106 RBIs, putting himself in position to pursue a second consecutive league MVP award. Ralph noted that the Phillies have been among the teams linked to Sato. And MLB insider Jon Heyman has also reported that the Phillies are targeting him. Most recently, Japanese media reported that the Phillies had representatives in Japan to watch Sato in person. “On the field, (Sato) led the team to its first-ever consecutive Central League championships and won the Triple Crown,” Yahoo! Japan noted in a translated report published last week . “On this day, scouts from the (Texas) Rangers, Phillies, and other American teams were also in attendance.” FORBES | By Peter Chawaga Dodgers Veteran Backstop Cuts Ties With Team Immediately After Season Ends Philadelphia Phillies Face Major Free Agency Decision After Teruaki Sato News Sato primarily plays third base, although he has also spent time in the outfield. His defensive versatility could give Philadelphia options as it evaluates how best to fit another impact hitter into its lineup. The Japanese star has also demonstrated sustained power beyond his Triple Crown season. He hit 40 home runs in 2025, when he earned Central League MVP honors. The posting process will give MLB clubs a limited window to negotiate with Sato once he officially enters the system. Under the rules outlined by Ralph, teams will have 45 days to reach an agreement, with Hanshin receiving compensation based on the value of his contract. For Philadelphia, the opportunity could address a growing need for offensive production while adding a younger player to an aging core. Whether the Phillies ultimately pursue Sato remains uncertain, but his availability gives the front office another high-profile option as it tries to turn another postseason disappointment into a championship run. This article was originally published on Forbes.com

item.title: Red Bull Is Going Full Ford Raptor for the US Grand Prix—Down to Verstappen’s Cowboy-Hat Helmet
item.description: Red Bull Racing’s F1 drivers are set to sport a special look for this weekend’s United States Grand Prix at the Circuit of the Americas (COTA) in Austin, Texas. Embracing the race’s cowboy-inspired theme, both Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar have donned white racing suits inspired by the Ford Raptor pickup truck. The four-time world champion takes things a step further with a new helmet featuring a cowboy hat design. Verstappen also posed alongside the pickup, adding another distinctly American touch to the team’s race-weekend preparations. According to a report by GPBlog , Red Bull’s USGP transformation goes beyond the cars and drivers, bringing the entire team into the spirit of American motorsport. Created alongside official kit partner Castore, the special-edition apparel takes cues from Ford’s performance off-road lineup. Team members will sport coordinated outfits, while the garage will also get a themed makeover inspired by the Raptor. Image Credit: Red Bull Racing / Instagram As race weekend approaches, Red Bull has been sharing promotional content on social media featuring both drivers in their special outfits. The white racing suits should help Verstappen and Hadjar stand out from the rest of the grid, unless other teams opt for white or similar shades for the USGP, such as their junior team, Racing Bulls. The campaign embraces a sort of wild west theme, with both drivers posing against a backdrop of flying dirt and rugged terrain. A dirt road, a Ford Raptor pickup truck, ropes, and cowboy hats complete the look, while warm sunset tones tie the entire scene together. Verstappen’s helmet retains the familiar Red Bull colors, with a greater emphasis on white to match the team’s special USGP look. What really sets the design apart, however, is the cowboy hat printed on the crown, seemingly worn by a roaring lion graphic that adds a fierce touch to the theme. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Oracle Red Bull Racing (@redbullracing) View this post on Instagram A post shared by Oracle Red Bull Racing (@redbullracing) Verstappen heads into the USGP in strong form after winning the Bahrain and Singapore GPs. He will be looking to make it three consecutive victories, especially with COTA proving to be a successful hunting ground for him after his win there last year. Red Bull’s recent improvements to the RB22 have also helped boost the team’s performance, potentially putting Verstappen in a strong position to challenge for another win this weekend. Get ready to suit up, partner https://t.co/kWMglfuUSn — Oracle Red Bull Racing (@redbullracing) October 15, 2026

item.title: ‘They deserved it’ – Anthony Gordon says PSG had ‘more quality’ than Barcelona
item.description: PARIS, FRANCE - OCTOBER 20: Anthony Gordon of FC Barcelona looks on during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Paris Saint-Germain and FC Barcelona at Parc des Princes on October 20, 2026 in Paris, France. (Photo by Pedro Salado/Getty Images) | Getty Images Anthony Gordon admitted he wasn’t at his best on Tuesday night as Barcelona slumped to a 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. The winger started the game but struggled to make much impact as an attacking force and was beaten by Lucas Hernandez for PSG’s second goal. Speaking afterwards, Gordon told TNT Sports he can do much better: “Ultimately, I didn’t think my performance was great tonight. “I’ve got a lot of individual work to do because on these nights, I really want to perform and I don’t think tonight I was at my best. “I think they deserved it in the end. I feel like they were the better team. They had better moments with more quality and I feel like athletically they were able to sustain the pressure, the intensity for longer than we were.” Gordon also spoke about the intensity of the game and how Barca need to find a way to improve so they can match PSG going forward. “They’re the best team in the world and have been for two years. We’re also a top team and we’ve had a great start,” he told CBS Sports. “It knocks us down a step but that’s a good thing because it gives us that drive back again that we need to beat them, we need to become the team to beat. “It’s exactly how it looks. It’s chaotic. I was so tired in the first 10 minutes and got more and more tired as the game went on. But it’s a great game, I prefer to play this style because I know it’s exciting, there’s more chances, it’s a better game to watch but yes I’m extremely tired now. “Life in Barcelona has been great. I’ve had a good start. But I’m nowhere near where I want to be, I can do so much more. People haven’t seen anyway near the best of me and it’s up to me to show them.”

item.title: PSG suffer major injury blow as Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tears ACL in Barcelona victory
item.description: PSG suffer major injury blow as Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tears ACL in Barcelona victory Paris Saint-Germain have confirmed that Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament during Tuesday’s Champions League victory over Barcelona. The Georgian winger sustained the injury to his right knee during PSG’s 4-2 triumph at the Parc des Princes and will undergo surgery in the coming days. The setback threatens to rule the 25-year-old out for the remainder of the campaign, dealing a significant blow to Luis Enrique’s European ambitions. Kvaratskhelia was forced off shortly before the hour mark after landing awkwardly while attempting to challenge Barcelona defender Xavi Espart. The former Napoli attacker appeared in considerable discomfort and required assistance from the medical staff after struggling to put weight on his right leg. Subsequent examinations confirmed the severity of the injury, with PSG announcing the diagnosis in an official medical update on Wednesday. “Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days,” the club stated. PSG have not provided a definitive recovery timeline, although ACL injuries typically require several months of rehabilitation. The development represents a considerable setback for Kvaratskhelia, who has established himself as one of Europe’s leading attackers since joining PSG from Napoli in January 2025. He played an influential role in the French champions’ recent European successes and was named the Champions League’s player of the season last term. PSG confirm further injury setbacks for Dembele and Marquinhos Kvaratskhelia’s injury compounds PSG’s concerns after Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos also sustained problems during the Barcelona encounter. Dembele was withdrawn in the 19th minute after suffering an injury to his left thigh, while captain Marquinhos departed around the hour mark with a right-thigh problem. PSG confirmed that both players will continue receiving treatment over the coming weeks, leaving Enrique without three important first-team figures. The French champions were already missing left-back Nuno Mendes, who sustained a thigh injury during their recent Ligue 1 victory over Strasbourg. Despite the setbacks, PSG secured an impressive victory over Barcelona through goals from Desire Doue, Lucas Hernandez, Vitinha and Fabian Ruiz. The result maintained their perfect Champions League record, with nine points collected from their opening three matches. However, Kvaratskhelia’s potentially season-ending absence leaves PSG facing a significant challenge as they pursue another European title.

item.title: Why Udogie missed Tottenham’s 3-1 win over Coventry City
item.description: Why Udogie missed Tottenham’s 3-1 win over Coventry City Italy international Destiny Udogie didn’t feature in Tottenham’s 3-1 win over Coventry City because of a knee problem: ‘We didn’t take a risk alongside the medical staff,’ Roberto De Zerbi explained. Italy international Udogie is dealing with a knee problem that kept him out of Tottenham’s 3-1 win over Coventry on Monday. The former Udinese defender was substituted off during a 1-1 draw against Manchester United the previous weekend. IPSWICH, ENGLAND – FEBRUARY 22: Destiny Udogie of Tottenham Hotspur takes on Jaden Philogene of Ipswich Town during the Premier League match between Ipswich Town FC and Tottenham Hotspur FC at Portman Road on February 22, 2025 in Ipswich, England. (Photo by Paul Harding/Getty Images) “Udogie played 70 minutes (against Manchester United) and suffered a problem of (the) knee, and we didn’t take a risk alongside the medical staff,” De Zerbi said via the Tottenham official website. Udogie, 23, has made six appearances across all competitions for Tottenham this season, collecting 283 minutes on the pitch. LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 15: Roberto De Zerbi, Manager of Tottenham Hotspur, looks on before the Carabao Cup Third Round match between Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur at Anfield on September 15, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images) The Italian left-back made his senior Azzurri debut in 2023 under Luciano Spalletti and has since featured 12 times for the national team. It remains to be seen whether Udogie will return to action in time for the next international break in November and whether Roberto Mancini will give him a chance. DORTMUND, GERMANY – MARCH 23: Destiny Udogie of Italy battles for possession with Antonio Ruediger of Germany during the UEFA Nations League Quarterfinal Leg Two match between Germany and Italy at Football Stadium Dortmund on March 23, 2025 in Dortmund, Germany. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) He last featured for the Azzurri in June 2025, when Italy lost 3-0 to Norway in a World Cup qualifier. Another left-back in the Premier League, Matteo Ruggeri, surely won’t be available for the Azzurri, as the Aston Villa defender faces a month on the sidelines with a hamstring injury.
