(Photo by Paul Harding/Getty Images) “Udogie played 70 minutes (against Manchester United) and suffered a problem of (the) knee, and we didn’t take a risk alongside the medical staff,” De Zerbi said via the Tottenham official website. Udogie, 23, has made six appearances across all competitions for Tottenham this season, collecting 283 minutes on the pitch. LIVERPOOL, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 15: Roberto De Zerbi, Manager of Tottenham Hotspur, looks on before the Carabao Cup Third Round match between Liverpool and Tottenham Hotspur at Anfield on September 15, 2026 in Liverpool, England. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images) The Italian left-back made his senior Azzurri debut in 2023 under Luciano Spalletti and has since featured 12 times for the national team. It remains to be seen whether Udogie will return to action in time for the next international break in November and whether Roberto Mancini will give him a chance. DORTMUND, GERMANY – MARCH 23: Destiny Udogie of Italy battles for possession with Antonio Ruediger of Germany during the UEFA Nations League Quarterfinal Leg Two match between Germany and Italy at Football Stadium Dortmund on March 23, 2025 in Dortmund, Germany. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) He last featured for the Azzurri in June 2025, when Italy lost 3-0 to Norway in a World Cup qualifier. Another left-back in the Premier League, Matteo Ruggeri, surely won’t be available for the Azzurri, as the Aston Villa defender faces a month on the sidelines with a hamstring injury.

item.title: What Tiger Woods did straight after a golf lesson which is recommended for amateurs to copy now
item.description: Photo by Simon Bruty/Anychance/Getty Images Butch Harmon has revealed that slow motion swings were the key to Tiger Woods working on the changes within his game after his first major win, and believes that amateur golfers should do similar after they have had a lesson. Harmon played a crucial role in taking Woods to the very top of the game. He was his coach for much of his amateur career before continuing to work with him until the early 2000s. Woods won his first eight majors during their partnership. He also completed the Tiger Slam in 2001, where he held all four majors at the same time. One of the most intriguing moments of Woods’ career came in the months after he won The Masters by 12 shots in 1997. At that stage, it appeared that there was nothing that the boy wonder could not do. However, Woods decided that he wanted to overhaul his swing. And while it meant that he had to wait more than two years for his second major title, it went on to reap huge rewards. Butch Harmon reveals how Tiger Woods learned to change his golf swing No golfer can comprehend playing that well and still waiting to start all over. However, Harmon thinks that most amateurs can take something from how Woods went about making those changes. Speaking to No Laying Up , Harmon revealed that slowing everything down on the practice ground was key to Woods creating his new swing. “Think about ’98, he won one time. One, it’s all he won in 1998. He spent a whole year working on changes to his swing. Then came ’99, 2000, ’01, ’02, the rest is history. And I tell people that I give a lesson to all the time, and you guys can relate to this if you take a lesson from your local PGA pro, it’s going to take time, change takes time. When you go out and you don’t play good, you just throw it out. ‘Well, that’s not working’,” he said. “Here’s the greatest player who ever lived, working harder than anybody who ever lived, and it took him about seven months to feel comfortable. I got a call from him one day on the range, it may have been around August, September, and he says, ‘okay Butch, I got it. I really got it now, right where I want it, everything’s good, the film looks good. I’m sending you the film’. He says, ‘everything was perfect’. And he was right. But he worked so hard on that. I wanted to do a little bit at a time. ‘No, I want to do it all right now’. “A lot of you who are watching this show who take lessons, I’m going to tell you something he did that I think would help you when you take lessons. He must have hit balls with a slow motion swing a thousand times, just making a full swing in slow motion to put the hands and arms and body rotation in the same position every time where he could feel that he was trying to go. “The average person, those of you who are watching, you can learn from that. Slow motion swings are a fabulous way for a player to feel what they’re trying to do, because in slow motion you can literally get your hands and arms and body in the right place.

However, Harmon thinks that most amateurs can take something from how Woods went about making those changes. And I tell people that I give a lesson to all the time, and you guys can relate to this if you take a lesson from your local PGA pro, it’s going to take time, change takes time. When you go out and you don’t play good, you just throw it out. ‘Well, that’s not working’,” he said. “Here’s the greatest player who ever lived, working harder than anybody who ever lived, and it took him about seven months to feel comfortable. I got a call from him one day on the range, it may have been around August, September, and he says, ‘okay Butch, I got it. I really got it now, right where I want it, everything’s good, the film looks good. I’m sending you the film’. He says, ‘everything was perfect’. And he was right. But he worked so hard on that. Slow motion swings are a fabulous way for a player to feel what they’re trying to do, because in slow motion you can literally get your hands and arms and body in the right place. You can feel yourself coming down and how you come through the shot, and film it.” The saying Tiger Woods used to have before a round during his peak It is difficult to imagine what the experience of playing in Woods’ era must have been like. Everyone in the field knew that Woods was going to be unbeatable if he was anywhere near his best. And it would appear that Woods fed off that aura to make him feel invincible. Harmon shared what Woods used to say to him on the range when he was at the peak of his powers. “I’ve seen the great players play, and I’ve never seen anybody control a ball like he did in 2000. Through the air, he had everything. He worked so hard on his wedge play, his short iron stuff with the three-quarter shots, he hit them all the time. Everybody talks about the shot out of the rough on six, to get up over the hill there. He took that six iron and just nuked it as hard as he could swing, got it up on the green and I think Roger Maltbie said, ‘this isn’t a fair fight’. He was amazing,” he said. “He had a saying. He’s probably not going to like that I’m going to tell you this. He had a saying that he used to tell Stevie and I on the range. He goes, ‘I know that they know that I know they can’t beat me’. And that’s a hell of a saying. That was his mentality.” Harmon must have felt enormous pressure working with Woods. Everyone felt that they knew what he was capable of once he won The Masters by a record margin 29 years ago. However, the pair swiftly set to work on substantial changes. Golf has seen numerous players, including major champions, almost ruin their game because of their belief that their swing needs to be overhauled. Had Woods gone on and not won another major, Harmon would have taken all sorts of criticism. And he would have been well aware of that during that wait for Woods’ victory at the 1999 PGA Championship. It says a lot about the two men that they never lost faith that they were making the right decision.

South Africa vs. Australia 2nd Test: Day 3 Live updates At Stumps: South Africa 425/9 (d), Australia 3/1 A day that began with South Africa cornered at 97/5 ended in a complete role reversal, as an extraordinary 179 from captain Temba Bavuma and an 82-run rear-guard masterclass from Simon Harmer lifted the Proteas to 425/9 declared before Kagiso Rabada removed Nic Maddinson for a duck in fading light to leave Australia 3/1 in 4.0 overs at stumps on Day 3. Bavuma spent over nine hours (552 minutes) at the crease, facing 334 balls for his 179. He was flawless on the drive and punch, finding 18 boundaries and clearing the ropes once off Pat Cummins. When Marnus Labuschagne finally breached Harmer’s defense at 425/8 and Starc had Bavuma caught behind on the very next ball, South Africa called time on the innings. Australia sent in five-wicket hero Scott Boland (2* off 13) after Maddinson departed alongside Travis Head (1* off 7). The pair navigated Harmer and Markram under gloomy skies until the umpires deemed the light unsuitable at 5:38 PM. At Tea: South Africa 318/7 Pat Cummins took the second new ball after 80 overs and immediately turned to his chief destroyer. Scott Boland struck on the fifth ball of the 81st over to dismiss Jansen for 85 (caught by Travis Head), securing his five-wicket haul (5/63) and breaking the dangerous stand at 242/7. Bavuma stood as an immovable rock. Shrugging off body blows and playing authoritative front-foot punches through the covers, the skipper brought up a hard-earned century off 226 balls (11 fours, 1 six). Simon Harmer proved an exceptional partner after Jansen’s departure, striking six boundaries in his 30* off 68 balls. The duo shared an unbroken 76-run stand for the 8th wicket, taking the Proteas past the 300-run mark in the 97th over. At Lunch: South Africa 216/6 Mitchell Starc completed 450 Test wickets as he got rid off Wian Mulder earlier in the day. Temba Bavuma is inching closer to a century as South Africa manage to cross the 200-run mark in the first session on Day 3. 450 Test wickets for Mitchell Aaron Starc 🥹🐐 At 36, the man has sacrificed money, fame and everything in between for the Baggy Green 🇦🇺 The 6th-fastest to reach the milestone, doing so in just 109 Tests ❤️‍🔥 #SAvAUS https://t.co/YHsNkdtAAH — CricketNews.com (@cricketnews_com) October 20, 2026 Good news for cricket fans across the world as it's not raining anymore in Gqeberha. It's a perfect morning for cricket. South Africa vs. Australia 2nd Test: Day 2 updates Skipper Temba Bavuma has played a lone hand of supreme discipline. He played 108 balls for his unbeaten 41 (5 fours, 1 six), anchoring the innings with immaculate judgement outside off stump. Walking in at 40/4, Ryan Rickelton struck five crisp boundaries to inject momentum. His 50-run stand with Bavuma took 99 balls and gave South Africa their only sustained partnership. Having struck twice before the rain on Day 1, Scott Boland remained virtually unplayable in helpful conditions. After accounting for Marques Ackerman (6) earlier in the day, he returned late in the afternoon to break a dangerous 52-run alliance, inducing an edge from Ryan Rickelton (31 off 51) to Matt Renshaw at 92/5 to claim his fourth wicket. Proteas captain Temba Bavuma has served as the lone bulwark against the Australian pacers, batting with compact technique to compile an unbeaten 29* off 77 balls with five boundaries. Mitchell Starc found extra bounce and movement to remove Matthew Breetzke for 4 in the 22nd over. Breetzke nibbled at an away-seamer, handing Carey his third catch of the innings as the hosts slumped to 40/4. Resuming from the Day 1 rain interruption at 20/2, Scott Boland picked up right where he left off. In the 15th over, he produced another delivery angling across debutant Marques Ackerman (6 off 38), drawing an outside edge through to Alex Carey to leave South Africa 25/3. Australia tightened their vice-like grip on the opening session of Day 2, striking twice through Scott Boland and Mitchell Starc to reduce South Africa to 62/4 in 30.1 overs at St George's Park. Play to resume soon at 3:45 pm local time. We might have just over 30.4 overs on day 2. Play remains suspended due to a wet outfield, with the next inspection at 3 pm local time. Players are still inside the pavilion, but there is some good news from the ground as the covers are reportedly coming off. It's still raining in Gqeberha, and there could be a delay in the start of Day 2. However, there is some positive update as the skies are expected to remain clear during the course of the day. South Africa vs. Australia 2nd Test: Day 1 updates At Stumps: South Africa 20/2 Persistent rain washed out the remainder of the opening day at St George's Park, with play officially called off and stumps drawn with South Africa locked at 20/2 in 11.5 overs. Scott Boland produced a sensational double-strike in the 9th over, removing both Aiden Markram and David Bedingham on consecutive deliveries to leave South Africa reeling at 20/2 in 11.5 overs before another persistent band of rain forced the players off the field on Day 1 at St George's Park.

item.title: Stephen A. Smith makes simple request to ESPN amid uncertainty around Troy Aikman’s future
item.description: Credit: Arturo Holmes/Mike Carlson via Getty Images ESPN’s flagship analyst Stephen A. Smith has weighed in on the brewing issues with the network’s flagship NFL broadcast team of Joe Buck and Troy Aikman. Buck and Aikman have been one of the best broadcast pairings in the NFL world, with the duo working together for over 20 years across different networks. They joined ESPN in 2022 and will be the broadcast duo for the network’s first Super Bowl in 2027. However, it looks like their partnership will end on a high, as ESPN has not solidified plans to bring both of them back next season. Buck had his contract extended until 2031, but Aikman’s status as a free agent at the end of the season has been causing major friction. Stephen A. Smith weighs in on Troy Aikman’s situation Smith, ESPN’s most notable on-air personality, discussed the Aikman-Bucks situation on his ‘Mad Dog Sports Radio’ show, expressing his desire to see Aikman stay with ESPN. “They are the A-team. Joe Buck, it don’t get no better, play-by-play. Excuse the double negative. It’s just the truth. And I feel the exact same way about Troy Aikman, who I love, who I’ve loved for years. That’s their business, that’s ESPN’s business, that’s ABC’s business, and all of that. I know they’ll be calling the Super Bowl this year. “Troy Aikman is a three-time Super Bowl champion, an elite football mind whose credentials and resume is as impeccable as they come, and it speaks for itself. I sincerely hope that we don’t lose him as a person that’s employed by ESPN, but if we do lose him, I want to wish him all the happiness in the world if he decides to go elsewhere. Because football must have Troy Aikman’s voice in it, he’s that special of a guy and a football mind, and I sincerely hope that we keep him.” What is happening with Troy Aikman at ESPN? Aikman and Buck joined ESPN on five-year deals in 2022, which will expire after Super Bowl LXI in February 2027. Buck was handed a reported six-year, $108 million contract extension by the network to keep him until 2031, while Aikman has confirmed that ESPN hasn’t even started negotiations for a new contract with him. This differing contract status has reportedly strained the previously healthy relationship between Buck and Aikman. The pair reportedly had an argument before a Bills-Rams game in mid-October, with reports of the same leading to Aikman clarifying his position on radio. The former Cowboys QB has made it clear that he will explore his options at the end of the season. While a return to ESPN can’t be ruled out, it’s likely Aikman will be courted by networks like Prime Video and CBS, with ESPN replacing Aikman with potentially a different former NFL legend-turned-commentator. item.title: Chiefs News: Mecole Hardman signs with Colts practice squad
item.description: (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs have plenty of rumors swirling about receiver reunions. One already happened: wide receiver Justin Watson signed to the practice squad and played one offensive snap and three special teams snaps after being elevated to the game-day roster for the win over the Los Angeles Chargers . We all know a Tyreek Hill signing is looming, though it’s not as inevitable as it once was. Trade rumors are swirling around Hollywood Brown after he hasn’t done much for the Philadelphia Eagles this season. One potential reunion with a former Kansas City speedster is now off the table — for now — with the Indianapolis Colts ’ practice-squad signing on Tuesday. The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Colts add WR Mecole Hardman, P Thomas Morstead to practice squad | Pro Football Talk Hardman, a three-time Super Bowl champion with the Chiefs, was most recently with the Bills, though he was released at roster cuts in August. He appeared in just two games for Buffalo last season, rerunning two punts and one kickoff. Indianapolis has added Morstead after punter Rigoberto Sanchez had to exit Sunday’s loss to Tennessee due to a foot injury sustained on a blocked punt. Morstead appeared in all 17 games for San Francisco last season, averaging 43.6 yards on his 44 punts. The Chiefs’ offense is rolling. But they need to make one change | The Kansas City Star Walker has carried the football 11 times on plays originating inside the 5. He has scored on only two of them. He’s been stopped at the line of scrimmage or for a loss of yardage on seven of the 11 attempts. So it’s been more than three times as likely for the opponent to celebrate a stop in the backfield as it has been for the Chiefs to celebrate a touchdown. The Chiefs’ touchdown percentage on rushing plays inside the 5 — the 2 of 11 equals 18.2% — is the second-worst percentage in the league. The Steelers are the only team worse, though they’ve somehow managed to attempt only one run inside the 5. They are 0-for-1. He’s been stopped at the line of scrimmage or for a loss of yardage on seven of the 11 attempts. So it’s been more than three times as likely for the opponent to celebrate a stop in the backfield as it has been for the Chiefs to celebrate a touchdown. The Chiefs’ touchdown percentage on rushing plays inside the 5 — the 2 of 11 equals 18.2% — is the second-worst percentage in the league. The Steelers are the only team worse, though they’ve somehow managed to attempt only one run inside the 5. They are 0-for-1. Chiefs Stock Watch: Who Helped and Hurt Their Case in Week 6 Win vs. Chargers? | Sports Illustrated Chiefs Stock Up After Week 6 Noah Gray Speaking of players who made the most of their opportunities in Week 6, Noah Gray matched the receiving output of Kelce by mustering 53 yards in the home win. Gray hauled in each of the three targets thrown his way and displayed some rare post-catch chops on a 31-yard rumble to boot. Kelce’s ankle injury limited his effectiveness and availability a bit, so Gray being the one to help insulate the pass catchers was a nice development. Denver Broncos – Kansas City Chiefs Week 8 game unlikely to be flexed to SNF | Mile High Sports he Chiefs face the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday Night Football this week. That seems like enough reason to not feature Kansas City on SNF in Week 8, or on back-to-back Sundays. But that’s not why Chiefs – Broncos won’t be on SNF in Week 8. According to Pro Football Talk, an NFL rule says these home-and-home games must be on Sunday afternoon. “By rule, at least one game of a home-and-home division rivalry must be televised on Sunday afternoon.” Chiefs Named Top Trade Destination for Projected $122 Million Star Playmaker | Heavy Sports “I might think … George Pickens is a trade candidate,” Solak detailed in an October 20, story titled, “Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 7: From Eagles to Matthew Stafford.” “His effort level and focus seem to be waning again, and the Cowboys will struggle to pay Pickens and cornerback Joey Porter Jr., whom they recently traded for,” Solak added. “If the 2-4 Cowboys keep losing games, I’d call Pickens on the franchise tag for the remainder of the season — we know he has game-breaking ability when he’s dialed in. Imagine Pickens in Los Angeles to help replace Davante Adams … or in Kansas City as Mahomes’ new downfield target? Exciting stuff.” Around the NFL Eagles won’t be punished for handling of Jalen Hurts’ blood clots: Source | The Athletic After further testing, within three days of returning to the U.S., the superficial blood clot had moved. Hurts has since been diagnosed with blood clots in both lungs and has been ruled out for the remainder of the NFL season. Hurts is clinically stable, but he can’t play football while on blood thinners, which his treatment requires. There have been many questions around the Eagles’ handling of Hurts. The NFL has been in regular communication with the team and its medical staff, the league source said. Giants releasing RB Najee Harris, source says | ESPN Harris, who is second on the team behind Cam Skattebo in rushing yards with 99 this season, got the start Sunday but had just four carries for 2 yards. That output ranked last of the six players who were credited with a carry for the Giants. Skattebo, who began the season as the team’s top running back, has seen his workload reduced after fumbling four times. In Sunday’s loss to the New Orleans Saints, Skattebo did not have a single carry. Titans release DT Jordan Elliott after ‘incident’ at team facility | CBS Sports Elliott’s surprising release is not the only strange occurrence the Titans are dealing with, as the team also made starting cornerback and $58 million free-agent addition Alontae Taylor inactive in Week 6. They didn’t just bench him; they took his uniform away. It was described as a coach’s decision, and Saleh has refused to elaborate on the situation. “We’ll discuss it as a staff and make a decision that is best for the team moving forward,” Saleh told reporters on Monday. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Is Harrison Butker a problem? Take the ‘Reacts’ survey Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker has missed three field goals this year. Of 27 NFL kickers with at least 10 field-goal attempts, he ranks 19th in field-goal percentage (76.9%). He has also missed a point-after attempt, with four misses through five games. item.title: PSG's Kvaratskhelia season in doubt after torn ACL
item.description: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffered an ACL injury during Paris Saint-Germain's win against Barcelona (JULIEN DE ROSA) Paris Saint-Germain could be without Khvicha Kvaratskhelia for the rest of the season after the winger tore his ACL in the Champions League win against Barcelona and Ousmane Dembele faces weeks out too, the club said on Wednesday. Both players suffered the injuries in the reigning European champions' 4-2 league phase win against Barcelona at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday. "Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday's match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days," PSG said in a statement, without giving a timeline for his recovery. Recovery from ACL surgery typically takes between six and nine months, meaning the 25-year-old Georgia international can at best hope to return for the closing stages of the season. Former Napoli winger Kvaratskhelia has established himself as one of Europe's most exciting attacking players and played a leading role in helping PSG to win back-to-back Champions League titles in the last two seasons. Like Dembele, he is one of the contenders for the Ballon d'Or, which will be awarded on Monday. The club said Dembele, the current Ballon d'Or holder, and influential Brazilian central defender Marquinhos will both be sidelined for "several weeks" with thigh injuries they suffered in the win against Barcelona. Kvaratskhelia slumped to the turf without any apparent contact and left the pitch just before the hour mark on Tuesday. Dembele, 29, had to be substituted after 20 minutes due to his injury. In the absence of two of their attacking stars, PSG will need to rely on summer signings Maghnes Akliouche, Mika Godts and Ferran Torres, the Spain international who scored the winning goal in the World Cup final in July. PSG are away to Ligue 1 leaders Lyon on Sunday in their next domestic match and they travel to Spanish side Villarreal for their next Champions League fixture on November 3. ali-rbo/gj/nf

item.title: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to undergo surgery after tearing ACL in PSG win over Barcelona
item.description: Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to undergo surgery after tearing ACL in PSG win over Barcelona Paris Saint-Germain have confirmed that Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has torn the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee and will undergo surgery, leaving the European champions without one of their most decisive attackers. The 25-year-old, who was named the Champions League's best player last season and is a nominee for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, was injured in Tuesday's 4-2 home win over Barcelona. The Georgia international landed awkwardly while challenging Barcelona full-back Xavi Espart just before the hour mark. He was helped off in the 59th minute and replaced by Maghenes Akliouche, with Espart and PSG teammate Desire Doue both trying to console him as he left the pitch. PSG said on Wednesday the operation will take place "in the coming days" but gave no recovery timeline, though it's likely the winger's season is over. "Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days," the club statement said. Kvaratskhelia joined PSG from Napoli in January 2025 and has scored 29 goals and provided 20 assists in 91 games for the club, playing an integral role in their back-to-back Champions League triumphs. Summer signing Mika Godts looks the likeliest candidate to replace Kvaratskhelia on the left wing, while Ferran Torresm, Ousmane Dembele and Akliouche offer alternative options. Dembele and Marquinhos also sidelined Kvaratskhelia was not the only casualty against Barcelona. Reigning Ballon d'Or holder Dembele went off with a left thigh injury in the 20th minute and was replaced by Torres, while captain Marquinhos hurt his right thigh soon after Kvaratskhelia's exit and made way for Ilya Zabarnyi. According to the club's statement, both players "will remain under treatment for the next few weeks". PSG, who are second in Ligue 1

item.title: Texas football fan banned after flipping off Florida players on field after UT loss
item.description: Florida players engaged in a postgame spat with a rowdy Texas football fan after Florida's 27-24 win in Austin on Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026. (Tim Warner/Getty Images) Texas football 's home contest against Florida last Saturday brought two losses for one Longhorns fan. Texas (4-2, 1-2 SEC) dropped its second straight game in a 27-24 defeat to the Gators, a surprising home loss that featured one additional moment of drama postgame. One person wearing a burnt orange polo was caught on video flipping his middle finger to a collection of Florida players. While some of the student-athletes laughed oof the gesture, a couple walked toward the fan before being separated by a team employee. Hated to see this after the game. Fans are frustrated but no need to run onto the field and do this. https://t.co/7aPogvnfyD - Anthony Geronimo (@ATXANT10) October 17, 2026 The fan, who appeared to have field access, has yet to be identified. But Texas athletic director Chris Del Conte announced Tuesday the person in question has been "permanently banned," from Royal-Memorial Stadium, the result of what Del Conte called a failure to "represent Texas with class and respect. GOLDEN : Steve Sarkisian deals with criticism that hits close to home "I want to address the video circulating on social media showing unacceptable behavior by an individual who had the privilege of field access following Saturday's game," Del Conte wrote in his weekly newsletter . "We pride ourselves on sportsmanship and treating our opponents with respect. This individual's actions did not reflect those values or meet our standards and will not be tolerated. "The matter has been addressed internally, and I want to personally apologize to the University of Florida and its entire football program. Having access to our field comes with a responsibility to represent Texas with class and respect. This individual failed to uphold that responsibility and has been permanently banned from Darrell K Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium." In his weekly newsletter, Texas athletic director Chris Del Conte formally addresses this past Saturday's postgame incident, announces that the unnamed individual has been banned permanently from DKR and apologizes to the Florida football team. #HookEm https://t.co/jdvTPGZzAr - Danny Davis (@_dannydavis) October 20, 2026 Texas will return to the field at DKR on Saturday night. Kickoff against No. 7 Ole Miss is set for 6:30 p.m. CT. Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. Start your day with the must-read headlines from Austin's most trusted news source. This article originally published at Texas football fan banned after flipping off Florida players on field after UT loss .

item.title: Lazio Fans Respond to Fabiani: “No Truce, We No Longer Want Lotito”
item.description: Lazio Fans Respond to Fabiani: “No Truce, We No Longer Want Lotito” The organised Lazio fan groups refuted Angelo Fabiani’s ‘truce’ plea, insisting that their protest will continue until Claudio Lotito leaves the club. The Background The supporters have been accusing the Italian senator of looking after his own interests rather than the club’s. They became increasingly irritated with the mismanagement of the accounts and the recurring sales of key players. Therefore, they have been refusing to attend Lazio’s home games at the Stadio Olimpico, instead accompanying the team on their travels. This decision is among several drastic measures taken to pile more pressure on Lotito’s administration and deprive him of important revenues. Lazio Enjoying a Stellar Start Despite the Protest Despite the chaotic situation, Gennaro Gattuso’s men have been enjoying a historic start to the campaign, registering six wins and one draw in the first seven rounds of the Serie A season. Hence, they currently share the top spot with defending champions and ultimate favourites, Inter Milan. Angelo Fabiani Urged Lazio Fans to Return to Stadio Olimpico Following Sunday’s ecstatic 3-0 win over Juventus in Turin, Lazio sporting director Fabiani sought the opportunity to urge the fans to return to the stands . The 63-year-old said the empty seats at the Olimpico have been giving him sleepless nights. He also argued that a ‘truce’ would be a huge morale boost for the players and Gattuso. Lazio Fans Turned Down Fabiani’s Truce Offer Shortly after Fabiani’s words were released, the organised Lazio fan groups firmly rejected the proposal through a statement announced on Radio Laziale (via La Lazio Siamo Noi ). The supporters insist that the team’s exploits won’t have any effect on their decision, as their battle against Lotito goes well beyond sporting results. The problem lies in Fabiani’s words. There is no truce to be signed; we do not have two different viewpoints. The point is that the fans no longer want that president. There can be no truce with someone you no longer want. Many newspapers want to reduce the protest to the team’s technical ability, but that is not the case. It is something much deeper-rooted, something that runs deep within us. We are absolutely delighted to be top of the table, and we hope to remain there until the end of the year. Lazio Have Found the Perfect Successors for Romagnoli & Gila – Opinion The organised supporters noted that they aren’t the only ones protesting against Lotito, but that the majority of the fanbase. It is not just the organised supporters who are emptying the stadium. They number 3,000 to 4,000 people. There are also smaller groups and pockets of supporters who have made the same choice. That is how you reach 45,000 people. Our protest is entirely justified, right and spontaneous. The other side does not want to admit it, but they spread false rumours and other things. The Background The supporters have been accusing the Italian senator of looking after his own interests rather than the club’s. The 63-year-old said the empty seats at the Olimpico have been giving him sleepless nights. He also argued that a ‘truce’ would be a huge morale boost for the players and Gattuso. The supporters insist that the team’s exploits won’t have any effect on their decision, as their battle against Lotito goes well beyond sporting results. The problem lies in Fabiani’s words. There is no truce to be signed; we do not have two different viewpoints. The point is that the fans no longer want that president. There can be no truce with someone you no longer want. Many newspapers want to reduce the protest to the team’s technical ability, but that is not the case. It is something much deeper-rooted, something that runs deep within us. We are absolutely delighted to be top of the table, and we hope to remain there until the end of the year. Lazio Have Found the Perfect Successors for Romagnoli & Gila – Opinion The organised supporters noted that they aren’t the only ones protesting against Lotito, but that the majority of the fanbase. It is not just the organised supporters who are emptying the stadium. They number 3,000 to 4,000 people. There are also smaller groups and pockets of supporters who have made the same choice. That is how you reach 45,000 people. Our protest is entirely justified, right and spontaneous. The other side does not want to admit it, but they spread false rumours and other things. When one side talks more than the other, it is clearly the side that is struggling. The Away Support Continues Finally, the Lazio supporters vowed to back the team in away games with large numbers, as they’ve been doing since the start of the season. We are always there. When we play away from home, there are never fewer than 5,000 of us. We are always giving the lads our support. We are all on their side; we cheer them on and support them. We are backing an entirely justified battle that goes far beyond the affection and esteem the players and the coach deserve. They deserve the world, more than many Lazio teams of the past. We are always there. Away from home, we make it feel like a home game for them. In Rome, however, there is a battle that is sacred, and the players know that. We have never asked them for anything.”

item.title: Premier League’s Biggest Spenders 2009-2018: Where Do Man City Rank?
item.description: Premier League’s Biggest Spenders 2009-2018: Where Do Man City Rank? Manchester City stepped into the lion’s den on October 11th when they travelled to a raucous Anfield to face Liverpool in the Premier League. The Blues were featuring in their first game since news of their run-in with the Premier League’s rule book broke, and they did so at the home of the one team that has suffered the most at City’s hands in recent times. But rather than suffering any kind of revenge, the visitors silenced those critics . City Down Liverpool at a Raucous Anfield Three sensational goals in 15 second-half minutes from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku, and Rayan Cherki, in front of a jubilant City away end, sealed a famous 3-0 at Anfield, ensuring that City’s perfect start to the 2026/27 Premier League season continued. Not only that, but online betting sites continue to make the club the biggest threat to Arsenal’s title defence. Ozoon soccer betting odds currently position Enzo Maresca’s side as a 7/2 second-favourite behind the 1/2 defending champion frontrunners, somewhat surprising odds considering City are currently two points clear at the summit. For the critics that continue to circle, the result was somewhat secondary to the situation the club currently finds itself in. Whether that’s sour grapes or not, however, remains to be seen. So, seeing as it’s all anyone seems to be talking about: That famous City spending that has landed the club in hot water. How much did the Blues splash in the transfer market between 2009/10 and 2017/18, the period currently in question? And how does it stack up compared to the Premier League’s biggest names throughout the same time frame? Let’s take a look. Manchester City — €1.44bn According to the highly reputable Transfermarkt , Manchester City forked out a whopping €1.44bn on new signings between 2009/10 and 2017/18. The spending was the most in Europe by over €300m, and the players that the club signed were a who’s who of bona fide superstars. Kevin De Bruyne was the most expensive addition. He arrived in January 2016 for a mighty fee of €76m (£54m), a club record at the time. Pundits such as Sky Sports legend Paul Merson were famously critical of the move, saying on one episode of Soccer Saturday: “I just don’t see £50million for this player.” How wrong he was. KDB would go on to become one of the greatest Premier League midfielders of all time, amassing some 108 goals and 177 assists in his decade at the Etihad, winning six titles and the Champions League as well. But as one can imagine with such spending, the Belgian wasn’t the only blockbuster arrival. Raheem Sterling arrived from Liverpool for €63.7m, John Stones from Everton for €55.6m, and Bernardo Silva from Monaco for €50m. But it wasn’t just the big names that City forked out huge sums on. Backup players such as Aymeric Laporte, Wilfried Bony, Eliaquim Mangala, and Danilo all arrived for at least €30m, with the Blues signing some 224 players throughout the eight-y

They are the only club in world football to have a net spend of over €1bn, and their approach yielded results: three Premier League titles, three League Cups, and an FA Cup are testament to that. Chelsea — €1.12bn But City weren’t the only ones spending big for those eight years. Chelsea also spent over €1bn as former owner Roman Abramovich looked to strengthen his side’s standing within European football. The billionaire had already forked out a fortune on new additions prior to the Premier League’s current financial rules coming into effect. He opened the chequebook to the amount of over €600m in the six years immediately preceding City’s questioned period, the most in Europe, with the likes of Andriy Shevchenko, Didier Drogba, Michael Essien, and many, many more arriving at the Bridge. Throughout the 2009/10 to 2017/18 period in question, the West London outfit wasn’t shy in splashing the cash. The January 2011 €58.5m move for Liverpool’s Fernando Torres was a British record at the time, while Alvaro Morata, Tiemoué Bakayoko, Michy Batshuayi, Diego Costa, Danny Drinkwater, and N’Golo Kante all cost €35m or more. Unsurprisingly, they too enjoyed success, winning three Premier League titles, three FA Cups, the League Cup, two Europa League crowns, and the 2012 Champions League . Manchester United — €1.01bn Manchester United spent over €1bn too, the fourth most in Europe behind City, Chelsea, and Barcelona, and they were smashing transfer records along the way. Their blockbuster €105m signing of Paul Pogba smashed the British transfer record, while Romelu Lukaku, Angel Di Maria, and Anthony Martial all cost over €60m each. The Difference Maker But the biggest difference between their spending and that of City is that these two Premier League heavyweights at least managed to recoup some cash in the form of sales. Chelsea sold players to the value of €689m, taking their net spend to €-426m, with Diego Costa, Oscar, and David Luiz all yielding over €49.5m. The Red Devils didn’t quite manage that number, with their sales totalling €385m. That took their net spend to €-621m, still some €300m better than that of their cross-city rivals.

item.title: ‘A Suspension Could Possibly Come,’ ‘Nobody Knows Entirely Where He Is Health-Wise’ — NFL Insider on Tyreek Hill’s Hurdles Amid Chiefs Reunion Talk
item.description: ‘A Suspension Could Possibly Come,’ ‘Nobody Knows Entirely Where He Is Health-Wise’ — NFL Insider on Tyreek Hill's Hurdles Amid Chiefs Reunion Talk Tyreek Hill’s road back to the NFL has more than one checkpoint, and not all of them are on a practice field. NFL insider James Palmer noted that “a suspension could possibly come if he signs with a team,” as the league keeps tabs on the 32-year-old free agent’s legal situation. That situation took a turn last week, when a Miami civil jury found Hill liable on two counts of battery involving his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro. However, with talk of a Kansas City Chiefs reunion still hanging around, the league office isn’t the only hurdle Palmer flagged. NFL Is Watching Tyreek Hill Even Without a Team Palmer brought Hill up with the Chiefs in mind, and the catch came quickly. “Everybody has Tyreek Hill circled because he’s played in it (the Chiefs’ system). You know what I mean? But there’s a lot going on with Tyreek. The NFL is continuing to monitor it, I’m told, directly by the league. Even though he’s a free agent, not on a team, they do continue to monitor his whole situation and gather all the information about what’s going on in his legal situation.” In the civil case, the jury tied the two battery counts to separate incidents in January 2024 and April 2025 and awarded Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages. It found Hill not liable on eight other claims, which included allegations of battery, assault, and continuing domestic violence, and declined to award punitive damages. Hill denied most of the allegations during the trial, although he acknowledged shoving Vaccaro during one incident. The NFL weighed in after the verdict with a statement to Pro Football Talk that squares with Palmer’s reporting: “We have been monitoring developments in the matter which remains under review of the personal conduct policy.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer That policy allows the league to review allegations of misconduct independently of the criminal justice system, and a civil finding of liability doesn’t automatically settle what discipline, if any, follows. Tyreek Hill’s Health and Where a Kansas City Chiefs Reunion Stands Then Palmer moved from the courtroom to the training room: “Nobody knows entirely where he is health-wise.” Hill’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, offered a sunnier read last week: “I don’t know that he’s 100% today, but he’s close, and he’ll get there really soon.” Hill hasn’t played since he dislocated his left knee and tore multiple ligaments, including his ACL, in the Miami Dolphins’ September 2025 game against the New York Jets. The injury required surgery and ended his season after four games, and the Dolphins released the eight-time Pro Bowler in February. He has shared videos documenting his recovery, but no timetable for his return has been confirmed. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Those questions follow Hill to any homecoming in Kansas

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Those questions follow Hill to any homecoming in Kansas City, where he helped win Super Bowl LIV before being traded to Miami in 2022. The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones took stock of the receiver room of a Chiefs team that is 5-0 and first in the AFC West, and of where a Hill reunion stands. Number two, as a wide receiver, you’d like to go to a team that needs a wide receiver. Number three, you’d like to go to a team that’s got a pretty good quarterback. And number four, Tyreek’s gonna bring a lot of impact. We’ve got to get a fair contract. And that’s always complex to negotiate in the middle of a season.” This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Barcelona starlet breaks Real Madrid legend’s Champions League record in memorable display vs PSG
item.description: Barcelona starlet breaks Real Madrid legend’s Champions League record in memorable display vs PSG Barcelona defender Xavi Espart has made history in the Champions League with the goal that he scored at Parc des Princes last night. The teenager became the youngest Spanish defender to score in the competition, surpassing a record previously held by Real Madrid legend Sergio Ramos. Espart achieved the milestone at just 19 years and 152 days, beating Ramos’ previous mark of 19 years and 251 days by 99 days. Espart makes history despite Barcelona’s defeat The achievement came during Barcelona’s 4-2 defeat against Paris Saint-Germain , a difficult evening for Hansi Flick’s side despite the individual milestone. Espart’s goal represents a significant moment in his young career, particularly given the level of opposition and the importance of the European stage. Xavi Espart impressed as a right-back against PSG. (Photo by Catherine Steenkeste for Qatar Airways/Getty Images) Surpassing Ramos is also noteworthy considering the former Real Madrid captain’s remarkable Champions League legacy. Espart’s performance last night yet again underlined the obvious quality he has and his readiness for this level. Another encouraging sign for La Masia Espart’s growing involvement comes at an important time for Barcelona, who are dealing with defensive injuries ahead of Sunday’s El Clasico . With Eric Garcia unavailable and Jules Kounde facing a race to recover, the youngster could have an important role against Real Madrid. His emergence gives Flick another option while demonstrating the value of Barcelona’s continued investment in academy development. However, scoring a historic Champions League goal is only one part of a defender’s development that is progressing at a rapid rate. Espart also showcased his ability to handle one-v-one situations against Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and later Desire Doue. The former, in particular, did not have any joy against the Barcelona teenager before being taken off with an injury. Considering the kind of form he is showing, it is easy to have massive expectations of the Spaniard ahead of upcoming games. However, Barça must be patient with his development and understand that things will not always go his way. Breaking a record held by Sergio Ramos is always an impressive early achievement, and it remains to be seen how he fares in the coming games.

item.title: Ringer faces emotional marathon one year after daughter's stillbirth
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Germany's Richard Ringer reacts at the finish line of the men's marathon during the Paris 2024 Olympic Games. (is associated with: «Ringer faces emotional marathon one year after daughter's stillbirth») Michael Kappeler/dpa Former European champion Richard Ringer has said he will run the Frankfurt Marathon on Sunday for his daughter who was stillborn a year ago. April Lucia Vivienne was stillborn on October 24, 2025, after Ringer and his wife were told two days earlier that the umbilical cord had become wrapped round their daughter’s little leg several times, preventing an adequate supply for the fetus. Ringer has been running for his daughter since then and that will especially be the case on October 25 when the Frankfurt race marks the first anniversary of the tragedy. "She will definitely be there. I will see that I will give my all for her again," Ringer told dpa, admitting the race "won't be easy mentally." Ringer said that he always thinks of his daughter when he runs and that he and his partner, German-Austrian runner Nada Ida Pauer, "try to do everything in such a way that she is proud of us. "Running definitely helped me deal with it," he said. Ringer and Pauer went public with the tragic news via Instagram, and Ringer said is was the right decision in retrospect because "we got a lot of support. That certainly did a world of good." Ringer won the European title in 2022 and is a co-favourite for first place in Frankfurt where the two other German top runners, reigning European champion and national record holder Amanal Petros and Samuel Fitwi, are also present. Petros' best is 2 hours 4 minutes 3 seconds, Fitwi's 2:04:45 and Ringer's 2:05:46. Ringer hopes to improve his personal best while challenging for the German record will also depend on how Petros and Fitwi do. All three are competing just two months after the Euros where Petros won, Fitwi was ninth and Ringer 10th. "Amanal, Samuel and I made a conscious decision to embark on this adventure with only a short preparation period because we were determined to perform in Germany once more,” Ringer said.

item.title: PSG’s Kvaratskhelia Set For Long Absence With Torn ACL
item.description: Paris Saint-Germain winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia requires surgery after tearing his ACL in the Champions League win against Barcelona, the European champions, said on Wednesday. “Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days,” PSG said in a statement. PSG’s Georgian forward Khvicha Kvaratskhelia lies on the pitch after sustaining an injury during the UEFA Champions League first round day 3 football match between Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) and FC Barcelona at the Parc des Princes stadium in Paris on October 20, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) In more bad news for PSG, the club said forward Ousmane Dembele and central defender Marquinhos will both be sidelined for “several weeks” with injuries. Kvaratskhelia slumped to the turf without any apparent contact and left the pitch just before the hour mark in the 4-2 league phase victory against Barcelona at the Parc des Princes on Tuesday. The 25-year-old Georgia international played a leading role in helping PSG to win back-to-back Champions League titles and is one of the contenders for the Ballon d’Or, which will be awarded on Monday. Dembele, the current Ballon d’Or holder, and Marquinhos both suffered thigh injuries, PSG said. Vitinha’s superb late strike proved crucial as reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain saw off rivals Barcelona 4-2 on Tuesday in a dramatic game between two of the leading contenders to win this season’s Champions League. The match was poised at 2-2 when the Portuguese playmaker, who came third in last year’s Ballon d’Or ranking, controlled on his chest and fired in from just outside the box in the 81st minute at the Parc des Princes. AFP The post PSG’s Kvaratskhelia Set For Long Absence With Torn ACL appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Nigeria already a failed state, middle class gone — Duke
item.description: PRP candidate blames poverty, unemployment for kidnapping, banditry The presidential candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Donald Duke, has described Nigeria as a failed state, citing worsening poverty, unemployment, insecurity and economic decline. Duke said he decided to contest the 2027 presidential election because he could no longer remain on the sidelines while the country’s challenges deepened without offering himself as an alternative. Speaking in an interview on Tuesday, the former Cross River State governor said he was driven by what he described as the urgency of rescuing Nigeria from its current trajectory. “You get to a point in your life where you say, ‘Either I walk away or I do something.’ “There is no guarantee that you will win. But I don’t want to look back and say that all these things happened and I did nothing,” he said. Duke said Nigeria could not afford another four years of what he described as its present economic and social decline. “I talk about the urgency of now because I don’t think we can go on like this for another four years,” he said. He added that his campaign would focus on policy options and solutions to the country’s challenges rather than personalities. “What I want to do is focus on those who aspire to lead this nation on addressing the issues that affect us and how we can resolve them. “I talk about the options. I talk about the real issues. I don’t want to talk about personalities,” he said. On insecurity, Duke argued that Nigeria’s security challenges could not be separated from the economy’s failure to create enough opportunities for its growing population. “If we don’t address these issues squarely and fundamentally, we’re already a failed state. There’s no question about it. “Look at what is happening — banditry, terrorism, kidnapping and all sorts of conflicts. These are symptoms of a state that is unable, not only to properly articulate its challenges, but to deal with them,” he said. Explaining his assessment, Duke said the existence of a government and public institutions did not necessarily mean that a state was meeting its responsibilities to citizens. “What is the definition of a failed state? Fundamentally, it is a state that fails to meet the aspirations of its people. “You may still have a government and institutions, but if the state cannot protect the people and provide the environment in which they can live productive lives, then it is failing them,” he said. item.content:encoded: PRP candidate blames poverty, unemployment for kidnapping, banditry The presidential candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party (PRP), Donald Duke, has described Nigeria as a failed state, citing worsening poverty, unemployment, insecurity and economic decline. Duke said he decided to contest the 2027 presidential election because he could no longer remain on the sidelines while the country’s challenges deepened without offering himself as an alternative. Speaking in an interview on Tuesday, the former Cross River State governor said he was driven by what he described as the urgency of rescuing Nigeria from its current trajectory. “You get to a point in your life where you say, ‘Either I walk away or I do something.’ “There is no guarantee that you will win. But I don’t want to look back and say that all these things happened and I did nothing,” he said. Duke said Nigeria could not afford another four years of what he described as its present economic and social decline. “I talk about the urgency of now because I don’t think we can go on like this for another four years,” he said. He added that his campaign would focus on policy options and solutions to the country’s challenges rather than personalities. “What I want to do is focus on those who aspire to lead this nation on addressing the issues that affect us and how we can resolve them. “I talk about the options. I talk about the real issues. I don’t want to talk about personalities,” he said. On insecurity, Duke argued that Nigeria’s security challenges could not be separated from the economy’s failure to create enough opportunities for its growing population. “If we don’t address these issues squarely and fundamentally, we’re already a failed state. There’s no question about it. “Look at what is happening — banditry, terrorism, kidnapping and all sorts of conflicts. These are symptoms of a state that is unable, not only to properly articulate its challenges, but to deal with them,” he said. Explaining his assessment, Duke said the existence of a government and public institutions did not necessarily mean that a state was meeting its responsibilities to citizens. “What is the definition of a failed state? Fundamentally, it is a state that fails to meet the aspirations of its people. “You may still have a government and institutions, but if the state cannot protect the people and provide the environment in which they can live productive lives, then it is failing them,” he said. He added that victims of kidnapping would have little reason to be concerned about academic debates over the definition of a failed state when they had experienced the consequences of insecurity. “Talk to someone who has been kidnapped. That person does not need you to explain the definition of a failed state. His experience has already told him what failure of the state means,” he said. Middle class disappearing Duke also lamented what he described as the virtual disappearance of Nigeria’s middle class, arguing that economic pressures had left many households struggling to meet their daily needs. “You have perhaps one per cent who are genuinely wealthy and then a huge number of people struggling around or below the poverty line. “The so-called middle class does not really exist anymore. Many of those we call middle class are only surviving from day-to-day. Let there be one serious emergency and they crumble,” he said. He said businesses were contracting while new enterprises were not emerging fast enough to absorb the growing number of people entering the labour market. “Businesses are contracting. New ones are not springing up the way they should. At the same time, we are turning out graduates every year and adding more people to the working population, but there is no work for them to do,” he said. The PRP candidate also linked poverty and unemployment to kidnapping and banditry, arguing that efforts to tackle insecurity would remain inadequate without addressing the underlying economic conditions. “When it comes to banditry and kidnapping, poverty and unemployment are at the bottom of much of it. “We keep reacting to these crises instead of asking what is producing them. We are too reactive in our governance. Governance is not just about today; it is about laying the foundation for tomorrow,” he said. Oil output, population growth Duke said another issue the presidential campaign should address was whether Nigeria’s economy had expanded sufficiently to support its growing population. Comparing the country’s crude oil production with its population growth, he said Nigeria’s economic capacity had not kept pace with the number of people it needed to support. “In 1980, Nigeria was producing about 2.5 million barrels of oil a day. Forty-six years later, we are producing around 1.7 million barrels, while our population has tripled. “So you have to ask: has the economy expanded enough to carry the population? Clearly, it has not,” he said. He argued that Nigeria’s population should be an economic asset if citizens had access to quality education, employment and opportunities to contribute productively to the economy. “Our numbers ought to be an asset. But a large population is an asset only when you can educate the people, employ them and make them productive,” he said. Duke warned that continued economic hardship could encourage more Nigerians with the means to emigrate, while those remaining in the country faced mounting pressure. Why I returned to Nigeria The presidential candidate said his ambition was also rooted in his decision decades ago to return to Nigeria after studying and working in the United States. “I had the opportunity in my twenties to remain in America. I went to school there and worked there for a while. “But I voluntarily decided that was not where I wanted to be. I believe the Almighty put me in Nigeria for a reason. I believe in this country’s possibilities, and this is where I believe I should contribute,” he said. Duke said the same conviction informed his decision to contest the Cross River governorship election in 1999 and had now motivated him to seek the country’s highest political office. “I wanted to prove then that we were better than what we were putting forward. From experience, I know Nigeria can be a very successful nation,” he said. The post Nigeria already a failed state, middle class gone — Duke appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: (Video) Liverpool fans will go wild over close-up footage of Ronald Araujo goal celebrations
item.description: (Video) Liverpool fans will go wild over close-up footage of Ronald Araujo goal celebrations The old mantra of ‘never fall in love with a loan player’ is proving very hard for Liverpool fans to follow in the case of Ronald Araujo. The Uruguayan defender – still technically a Barcelona player – is spending the season with the Reds and has quickly endeared himself to the Anfield faithful with his ebullient demeanour and wholly committed performances. He was substituted at half-time in the 4-3 win over Villarreal on Tuesday night, with Andoni Iraola attributing it to a tactical reshuffle rather than an injury , but not before scoring his team’s equaliser on the stroke of half-time. Araujo goal celebration captured with fan footage Araujo ghosted in behind the visitors’ defence to get on the end of a Rio Ngmuoha cross and steer a header into the net, with Sergi Cardona paying the price for letting the ball bounce rather than dealing with the danger. The Liverpool defender’s instant reaction was to leap into the crowd at the front of the Anfield Road Stand, and he was duly mobbed by exultant supporters in a moment which further enhanced his popularity with Kopites. Close-up footage of the goal celebrations shows just how many fans ran to the 27-year-old to salute him over the equaliser, in a viral clip that Reds everywhere will adore. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Will Araujo sign for Liverpool permanently? While Araujo’s performance last night was among his poorer ones for Liverpool so far, the close bond that he’s formed with supporters was underlined by the communal celebration for his equaliser. The Uruguayan told the media earlier this week that he’s quickly grown a strong affection for life on Merseyside, although he was non-committal when asked about the probability of his loan move becoming permanent. There’s still more than enough time for the necessary behind-the-scenes discussion to happen in that regard, but what we can say with certainty is that the Reds would likely be in much worse pace this season if they didn’t have the 27-year-old. His ability to cover at right-back has been massively important due to the long-term injury to Conor Bradley and the less than convincing form of the now-incapacitated Jeremie Frimpong. If Araujo does join Liverpool permanently over the next few months, Kopites are sure to be every bit as thrilled as they were with his equaliser last night. item.content:encoded: (Video) Liverpool fans will go wild over close-up footage of Ronald Araujo goal celebrations The old mantra of ‘never fall in love with a loan player’ is proving very hard for Liverpool fans to follow in the case of Ronald Araujo. The Uruguayan defender – still technically a Barcelona player – is spending the season with the Reds and has quickly endeared himself to the Anfield faithful with his ebullient demeanour and wholly committed performances. He was substituted at half-time in the 4-3 win over Villarreal on Tuesday night, with Andoni Iraola attributing it to a tactical reshuffle rather than an injury , but not before scoring his team’s equaliser on the stroke of half-time. Araujo goal celebration captured with fan footage Araujo ghosted in behind the visitors’ defence to get on the end of a Rio Ngmuoha cross and steer a header into the net, with Sergi Cardona paying the price for letting the ball bounce rather than dealing with the danger. The Liverpool defender’s instant reaction was to leap into the crowd at the front of the Anfield Road Stand, and he was duly mobbed by exultant supporters in a moment which further enhanced his popularity with Kopites. Close-up footage of the goal celebrations shows just how many fans ran to the 27-year-old to salute him over the equaliser, in a viral clip that Reds everywhere will adore. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Will Araujo sign for Liverpool permanently? While Araujo’s performance last night was among his poorer ones for Liverpool so far, the close bond that he’s formed with supporters was underlined by the communal celebration for his equaliser. The Uruguayan told the media earlier this week that he’s quickly grown a strong affection for life on Merseyside, although he was non-committal when asked about the probability of his loan move becoming permanent. There’s still more than enough time for the necessary behind-the-scenes discussion to happen in that regard, but what we can say with certainty is that the Reds would likely be in much worse pace this season if they didn’t have the 27-year-old. His ability to cover at right-back has been massively important due to the long-term injury to Conor Bradley and the less than convincing form of the now-incapacitated Jeremie Frimpong. If Araujo does join Liverpool permanently over the next few months, Kopites are sure to be every bit as thrilled as they were with his equaliser last night. item.title: Columbus Blue Jackets' meltdown lets Kirill Marchenko leave happy
item.description: It took a few seconds to recognize the song and pair it with the situation during Kirill Marchenko's victorious return to Nationwide Arena . More: Columbus Blue Jackets collapse again in 6-2 loss to Toronto Maple Leafs As the video board above center ice flipped from a "welcome back" photo to a live shot of Marchenko on the Toronto Maple Leafs ' bench, the sounds of CeeLo Green belting out lyrics to his most popular song, "Forget you," echoed in the building. "See you driving 'round town with the girl I love, and I'm like, 'Forget you!'" Green sings. "I guess the change in my pocket wasn't enough, I'm like, 'Forget you and forget her too! Said if I was richer, I'd still be with ya ..." It didn't take many notes for a raucous crowd to sing along after booing Marchenko with precision, only most didn't sing, "Forget you!" when the screen cut to a replay of Adam Fantilli blasting Marchenko with a body check. A much cruder version of the song's chorus was the preferred choice of those seated in the nosebleeds, and more than a few folks waved an R-rated hand gesture at the screen. Marchenko, of course, was unflappable. He tied the game 1-1 in the first period by going to the net for a deflection off his right skate, and that goal set the stage for the Leafs' surge in the second. It was foreshadowing for a 6-2 pasting the Blue Jackets (3-5-0) took while allowing four unanswered goals in the second periods of two ugly losses within a week. Perhaps Tuesday nights aren't agreeable? If so, check the upcoming schedule. The Blue Jackets are booked solid on Tuesdays until Thanksgiving, a time of year that often coincides with them exiting the playoff race. Marchenko, meanwhile, is as happy as a clam wearing blue and white. "It’s obviously special, fun, everything," he said afterward. "I’m happy to play here, happy to be back and thank you, again, for all fans, for everybody who’s been here when I was here for four years. I have only positive notes. So, it was a really good time, but, again, I am really happy to win the game. It’s so important to me.” Positive notes? Thank you, fans? Fun? Nothing about that game was fun for the Blue Jackets or their fans, save for Fantilli's heavy hip check on Marchenko and Jake Christiansen scoring his first goal since 2024. Everything else was reduced to bloviated bluster written on oversized checks the Blue Jackets couldn't cover. The same thing happened a week ago in a 7-3 loss to the Florida Panthers on Oct. 13 at Nationwide Arena, and coach Rick Bowness was excoriated by podcasters and studio analysts alike for saying the Blue Jackets should've felt embarrassed by it. This was even more humiliating, but Bowness bit his lip. The Maple Leafs had already played a game, and won, 24 hours earlier in Toronto. After flying to Columbus and getting in a nap, they backed up Marchenko in a hostile environment by skating circles around the Blue Jackets. Marchenko wasn't the only former Blue Jacket enjoying it, either. Jack Roslovic,

More: Columbus Blue Jackets collapse again in 6-2 loss to Toronto Maple Leafs As the video board above center ice flipped from a "welcome back" photo to a live shot of Marchenko on the Toronto Maple Leafs ' bench, the sounds of CeeLo Green belting out lyrics to his most popular song, "Forget you," echoed in the building. "See you driving 'round town with the girl I love, and I'm like, 'Forget you!'" Green sings. "I guess the change in my pocket wasn't enough, I'm like, 'Forget you and forget her too! Said if I was richer, I'd still be with ya ..." It didn't take many notes for a raucous crowd to sing along after booing Marchenko with precision, only most didn't sing, "Forget you!" when the screen cut to a replay of Adam Fantilli blasting Marchenko with a body check. A much cruder version of the song's chorus was the preferred choice of those seated in the nosebleeds, and more than a few folks waved an R-rated hand gesture at the screen. Marchenko, of course, was unflappable. He tied the game 1-1 in the first period by going to the net for a deflection off his right skate, and that goal set the stage for the Leafs' surge in the second. It was foreshadowing for a 6-2 pasting the Blue Jackets (3-5-0) took while allowing four unanswered goals in the second periods of two ugly losses within a week. Perhaps Tuesday nights aren't agreeable? If so, check the upcoming schedule. The Blue Jackets are booked solid on Tuesdays until Thanksgiving, a time of year that often coincides with them exiting the playoff race. Marchenko, meanwhile, is as happy as a clam wearing blue and white. "It’s obviously special, fun, everything," he said afterward. "I’m happy to play here, happy to be back and thank you, again, for all fans, for everybody who’s been here when I was here for four years. I have only positive notes. So, it was a really good time, but, again, I am really happy to win the game. It’s so important to me.” Positive notes? Thank you, fans? Fun? Nothing about that game was fun for the Blue Jackets or their fans, save for Fantilli's heavy hip check on Marchenko and Jake Christiansen scoring his first goal since 2024. Everything else was reduced to bloviated bluster written on oversized checks the Blue Jackets couldn't cover. The same thing happened a week ago in a 7-3 loss to the Florida Panthers on Oct. 13 at Nationwide Arena, and coach Rick Bowness was excoriated by podcasters and studio analysts alike for saying the Blue Jackets should've felt embarrassed by it. This was even more humiliating, but Bowness bit his lip. The Maple Leafs had already played a game, and won, 24 hours earlier in Toronto. After flying to Columbus and getting in a nap, they backed up Marchenko in a hostile environment by skating circles around the Blue Jackets. Marchenko wasn't the only former Blue Jacket enjoying it, either. Jack Roslovic, who's from Upper Arlington and spent four mostly miserable seasons with his hometown team, scored a goal against the Blue Jackets, per usual, and added two assists for fun. If you listened closely, you could probably hear former Blue Jackets goalie Elvis Merzlikins cackling from Switzerland while his former teammates put Jet Greaves, his replacement, in too many bad spots. That's happening too much, as the Blue Jackets spring leaks with careless stick penalties, unchecked forwards left alone in dangerous areas and ongoing special teams woes. The coaches change. The roster changes. The results stay the same. Perhaps that's part of the reason Marchenko forced his way out, and why it feels like only a matter of time before Zach Werenski does the same. "It's just stuff we need to figure out right now," center Charlie Coyle said. "It's stuff we should've figured out weeks ago, you know? It's just ... it's not good. It's not the right way to play. You see the results we get. That's a tired team that played last night [Oct. 19). There's no excuse [for] the way we played. [We] let Jet out to dry, a guy who's been there for us, standing on his head making saves. We left him out to dry, and it's a shame." The Blue Jackets also let Marchenko off the hook. Instead of sending a message that he prematurely left a promising team on the rise, the Jackets got hammered in their own rink and Marchenko left grinning despite the evening's hostilities. "Good hit [by Fantilli]," Marchenko said. "It was a couple guys who hit [me]. It was great. I take it. It’s fine. It’s a surprise, but it’s a good hit, actually, and I need to be aware next time, and head up quicker or maybe [shoot] quicker. ... I’m happy to win. Again, I can take so many hits when we win the game and have the two points. It’s all nice.” In other words, forget you. item.title: NFL Players Association calls for full investigation into Jalen Hurts’ medical care
item.description: The NFL Players Association is calling for full investigation into the Philadelphia Eagles' handling of quarterback Jalen Hurts’ blood clots after the NFL defended the way the situation was managed. The NFL Players Association said it is not aware of any league investigation into the medical care provided Hurts, adding that the NFL previously told the union it did not plan to review the care he received. “Before conclusions are drawn about how this situation was handled, there must be a full investigation into what occurred,” the NFLPA said. “Determining the facts is essential to ensuring players receive the highest level of care and protection going forward.” Alastair Grant/AP Photo - PHOTO: Jalen Hurts This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

item.title: Joshua Kimmich to miss Arsenal match following family tragedy
item.description: (Photo by F. Noever/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images Bayern Munich will face Arsenal at home in the group stage of the UEFA Champions League later today, but will do so without one of their most important players. Ahead of the clash, the club shared a somber update regarding the availability of Joshua Kimmich through their official X handle . The club announced that midfielder and vice-captain Joshua Kimmich will not be available for the game due to the passing of a close fami ly member: Due to a passing in his immediate family, Joshua Kimmich is not in the squad today for the match against Arsenal. On behalf of the family, we ask that his privacy and grief be respected, and that further inquiries and reporting be refrained from. We send our deepest condolences to Joshua Kimmich and his loved ones. Bild is reporting that Kimmich’s father, Berthold, has passed away: BILD has learned from sources close to him that the Bayern star and German international is mourning the sudden death of his father, Berthold (57). There are likely few things more important than football to Kimmich, but family is above all else. We wish Kimmich and his family strength to get through these tough times together. item.title: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander shows why he, not Wemby, is NBA's best player | Carlson
item.description: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander mean-mugged as he sat on the San Antonio hardwood, his gaze steely, his fists clenched, his arms flexed. His OKC Thunder teammates offered hands to help him up late in the third quarter, but instead, he slapped their palms in celebration of the shot he’d made and the foul he’d drawn. It was emphatic. It was confident. So was SGA on Tuesday night. He was the best player on the court — and it wasn’t particularly close. Neither was the game. Thunder 116, Spurs 104 . On the NBA’s opening night, all eyes were on this matchup. Oh, sure, there was a ring ceremony in New York. Yes, there was a first look at LeBron and the Sixers. But Thunder-Spurs was the marquee matchup . These ridiculously young but supremely talented teams are the preseason favorites to win the championship — and as that second-quarter dust-up showed, they aren't favorites of each other — but of course, both being in the Western Conference, they have to go through each other in the playoffs. TAKEAWAYS: Chet Holmgren shows no fear vs Victor Wembanyama, Spurs as Thunder rolls in opener The Spurs got the better of that matchup in last season, but if Tuesday is any indication, a fully healthy Thunder is more than capable of handling Wemby and Co. The biggest reason for that? Shai Gilgeous-Alexander remains the best player in the game. Now, there is going to come a time when Victor Wembanyama takes that title. He's too good, too unique, too game-changing. Seems way more a case of when, not if he wins MVPs. But Tuesday’s game is Exhibit A that Wemby isn’t there yet. Wemby’s stat line: 12 points on 1-of-13 shooting (yes, 1 of 13!), 13 rebounds, three assists and six blocks. SGA’s stat line: 32 points on 13-of-27 shooting, five rebounds, four assists and three blocks. Gilgeous-Alexander played all night like a man on a mission. Focused. Forceful. “Obviously, this is the team that eliminated us from achieving our goal,” he said in an on-court post-game interview with NBC after the game. “But for us, I think it was more, we’re just happy to be back. “It’s a long summer when you don’t win, and we felt that this summer.” SGA likely felt it on several levels. The two-time reigning MVP ended up carrying a heavy load after Jalen Williams and Ajay Mitchell went down with injuries, and for much of the Western Conference Finals, Gilgeous-Alexander struggled. His shot was off. His rhythm was, too. With the exception of Game 7 when he was spectacular, he wasn’t himself.
