The family of Othman Omar Abdelrazik and Omar Abkar Abdelrazik, who were killed in airstrikes on a gold mine on the Sudan-Egypt border on October 11, receive condolences at their home in Wad al-Hulaywah, Kassala State in eastern Sudan on October 16, 2026. The number is widely considered a conservative figure, with hundreds of miners — many of them children — still unaccounted for in the rugged mountains. Eleven have been reported killed from Hamdan’s tiny hometown of Wad al-Hulaywah alone. In the farming village near the Ethiopian border, AFP met the handful of survivors who made it home, and the bereaved families whose sons never will. Village In Mourning Another survivor, Omar Mohieddin, said people had initially relaxed when the aircraft disappeared from view. “They came every day or two, so people were used to them,” he told AFP. “When it flew north, everyone thought it had gone.” But it returned minutes later, and he said he could see “the Egyptian flag on it”. At the first explosion, Hamdan and three others threw themselves into a hole, he said. When he emerged, one of his comrades’ “insides were outside his body”. The village has been in mourning for a week. Groups of men in white jellabas sit shoulder to shoulder, their faces drawn with exhaustion and shock. This month’s strike occurred in the vast, mineral-rich mountains between Sudan and Egypt, which include the Halayeb Triangle claimed by both countries and controlled by Egypt. Egypt this year launched a military campaign to secure its southeastern desert from illicit gold mining and human trafficking. The first Egyptian airstrike in June reportedly killed 23 miners. Survivors of the latest strike had to walk for hours carrying the injured, while others died on the roadside “without food or water”, a doctor at a small clinic near the border told AFP. “The scenes were impossible to describe,” he told AFP. “People arrived in pieces, shrapnel wounds to eyes, heads, legs and chests. Some of the most seriously wounded never reached us because there was no way to transport them.” Abkar Mohamed Haron, 38, who was injured during airstrikes on a gold mine on the Sudan-Egypt border on October 11, receives treatment in Wad al-Hulaywah, Kassala State in eastern Sudan on October 16, 2026. Gold Or Guns Tarek Ahmed Issa, 19, had joined others hiding in mountain ridges after the strike. When they climbed down, there were corpses everywhere. “We buried the dead, but there were many others we couldn’t find,” he said. The teenager is still in the area, desperate for a way to transport “four months worth of work” to the nearest gold market to sell. “There are hardly any trucks,” and those that do come are charging double. The war has left young Sudanese — 25 million under 18, eight million of them out of school — with two main options to make a living: take up arms in one of the country’s many militias, or dig for gold. The multi-billion dollar gold industry depends on millions digging in dangerous, informal mines with their bare hands. Those who survive the mine collapses and aerial bombardment face a lifetime of diseases from the mercury and cyanide used to filter the precious metal — all to sell gold nuggets in local markets, at a fraction of global prices. “By the time the ore is sold, everyone takes a cut,” said Omar Abdelrazig Abdalla, who lost both his son and nephew in the attack. “You pay the truck owner, the refinery owner and others before you finally get your share.” Issa, the teenager hiding in the mountains, said he has no other option. “The war left us no farming and no livestock. I have to keep working so my family can survive.” AFP The post Sudanese Gold Miners Found ‘In Pieces’ After Egypt Border Airstrike appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Australian Lawmaker Loses Legs After ‘Targeted’ Attack
item.description: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has had both legs removed after what police called a “targeted” attack. Haines is in stable condition at a Melbourne hospital after being struck by a car on Monday near her office in the town of Wangaratta, more than 200 kilometres (120 miles) northeast of the Victoria state capital. Speaking at the hospital, her husband Phil told journalists on Wednesday that surgeons had been forced to remove both her legs. “But the good news in all this is Helen is alive, and she’s stable. That is the most important thing for our family,” he said. “The two most important parts of Helen for us as a family are her heart and her mind,” he said. “Her heart is huge. She is a very compassionate, caring, loving person.” Phil Haines, husband of Australian politician Helen Haines, who lost both legs in an attack, addresses the media with his cousin Jules Muir (L) during an update on Helen Haines’ condition at the Alfred Hospital in Melbourne on October 21, 2026. Photo by WILLIAM WEST / AFP The man alleged to have wounded Haines, in what police have called a “targeted” attack, faced court earlier on Wednesday. Police have charged 43-year-old Brendan Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison. He has also been charged with cultivating a cannabis plant and possession of the drug, according to court documents shared with AFP. Nugent appeared at a courthouse in Wangaratta. He did not apply for bail, and his next hearing is scheduled for February 4. ‘Extremist Views’ The alleged attack has sparked soul-searching in a country where political violence is rare, but where police have documented a steady rise in threats and abuse towards elected officials in recent years. This handout sketch by artist Anita Lester dated October 21, 2026, depicts 43-year-old Brendan Nugent at a court hearing in Wangaratta, after he was charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, after allegedly attacking Australian lawmaker Helen Haines, who was critically wounded in Wangaratta on October 19. Governor-General Sam Mostyn — King Charles III’s official representative in Australia — said the nation was crying out for “decency” following the attack. “Australians are yearning for kindness and care, and they’re asking us why we’ve lost the great skill of disagreeing well,” Mostyn said alongside Helen’s husband Phil. item.content:encoded: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has had both legs removed after what police called a “targeted” attack. Haines is in stable condition at a Melbourne hospital after being struck by a car on Monday near her office in the town of Wangaratta, more than 200 kilometres (120 miles) northeast of the Victoria state capital. Speaking at the hospital, her husband Phil told journalists on Wednesday that surgeons had been forced to remove both her legs. “But the good news in all this is Helen is alive, and she’s stable. That is the most important thing for our family,” he said. “The two most important parts of Helen for us as a family are her heart and her mind,” he said. “Her heart is huge. She is a very compassionate, caring, loving person.” Phil Haines, husband of Australian politician Helen Haines, who lost both legs in an attack, addresses the media with his cousin Jules Muir (L) during an update on Helen Haines’ condition at the Alfred Hospital in Melbourne on October 21, 2026. Photo by WILLIAM WEST / AFP The man alleged to have wounded Haines, in what police have called a “targeted” attack, faced court earlier on Wednesday. Police have charged 43-year-old Brendan Nugent with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, which carries a maximum penalty of 10 years in prison. He has also been charged with cultivating a cannabis plant and possession of the drug, according to court documents shared with AFP. Nugent appeared at a courthouse in Wangaratta. He did not apply for bail, and his next hearing is scheduled for February 4. ‘Extremist Views’ The alleged attack has sparked soul-searching in a country where political violence is rare, but where police have documented a steady rise in threats and abuse towards elected officials in recent years. This handout sketch by artist Anita Lester dated October 21, 2026, depicts 43-year-old Brendan Nugent at a court hearing in Wangaratta, after he was charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury and intentionally causing serious injury, as well as the federal crime of harming a public official, after allegedly attacking Australian lawmaker Helen Haines, who was critically wounded in Wangaratta on October 19. Governor-General Sam Mostyn — King Charles III’s official representative in Australia — said the nation was crying out for “decency” following the attack. “Australians are yearning for kindness and care, and they’re asking us why we’ve lost the great skill of disagreeing well,” Mostyn said alongside Helen’s husband Phil. The motive remains unknown, and authorities have refused to speculate while the investigation takes place. But police said Wednesday they were examining all possible leads, including that Nugent may have held radical anti-government views. “Like everyone, we’re examining social media associations, talking to witnesses, friends and colleagues,” Victoria police commissioner Mike Bush told journalists. Bush said authorities held no intelligence on the suspect and had seen nothing to suggest he posed an immediate threat before the attack. Australian Federal Police (AFP) Commissioner Krissy Barrett said there was a growing level of “extremist views” online. “The current criminal threat environment is febrile, and when it comes to federal parliamentarians, the AFP continues to record the growing volume of online abuse, threatening rhetoric and intimidation,” she said. World ‘More Dangerous’ The independent lawmaker, 65, was standing near the trunk of her car when she was struck by a Toyota Land Cruiser on Monday afternoon. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has led an outpouring of support for Haines, who was widely praised for her efforts to increase transparency in politics and crack down on corruption. He bemoaned the fact that political debate in Australia had grown too heated and personal over the past few years. “It’s a reminder that the world is a more dangerous and divided place than it was a generation ago,” Albanese told ABC Melbourne radio on Wednesday. “I think that Australians do want to see their politicians be able to go about their business, to be able to get something from the back of their car, for goodness sake.” Haines entered parliament in 2019 after working as a nurse and midwife, becoming known for stances such as supporting stronger climate action. item.title: France braces for more protests – security measures at a glance
item.description: After a weekend of protests, riots and looting, France is looking to head off further unrest, ahead of fresh demonstrations called for Saturday. Here are some of the measures authorities have ordered: – Curfews – Partial nighttime curfews were imposed in parts of Paris and several other cities on Monday and Tuesday nights, applied to areas where clashes broke out last weekend and shopping zones that had been targeted by looters. Paris also banned public gatherings on the Champs Elysees, near major public buildings, and near train stations. Marseille, France’s second-biggest city, has banned unaccompanied minors from central shopping streets every night up to and including Friday. – Bans – Paris police have banned people carrying bottles or cans of petrol or gas, or possessing fireworks, up to and including Thursday. Last weekend, youths set fire to several shops and public buildings, and shot fireworks through tubes at police, wounding several. – Deployment – French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has vowed a “massive” security deployment for Saturday, after his government admitted it “lost control” last weekend. President Emmanuel Macron on Sunday said authorities would be “uncompromising” towards “agitators from ultra-left fringe groups” that he blamed for much of the violence. Elite police units have been mobilised for the coming weekend. Macron has not, however, declared a state of emergency that would allow troops to be sent to reinforce police lines. However, soldiers who for more than a decade have been patrolling sensitive sites, airports and train stations and tourist zones under “Operation Sentinelle” would continue to be deployed to protect those spots. – Shops – The government has announced interest-free loans for 3,000 shops that were damaged, many of them looted, during last weekend’s unrest. Shop owners say that is not enough, though. Crowdfunding initiatives have sprung up on social media for residents to help their local shops rebuild. But the total amount being raised is only in the low hundreds of thousands of euros — whereas the sector says the damage bill will run to hundreds of millions. – Burnt bikes – Tourists visiting Paris right now hoping to use the usually ubiquitous rental bikes available via apps might find them a bit more scarce. More than 1,000 of the 40,000 bicycles deployed across the capital were destroyed, often burned, as they were thrown into makeshift street barricades built by protesters, according to an AFP tally of figures from the operators. – Food deliveries – Staying in and ordering food delivery could also be a problem for some. The Union-Independants union covering most delivery bike riders has asked Uber Eats, Deliveroo and other such companies to suspend deliveries to areas considered dangerous. It called for the riders to be able to cancel deliveries without losing money and for them to have a system allowing them to see risky areas in real time. item.title: All 'Stranded' keypad puzzle codes in Modern Warfare 4
item.description: There are eight keypad puzzle codes to solve during "Stranded" in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , but figuring out the number puzzles isn't easy. Inside each one, you'll find valuable supplies and equipment that will help you take down the three mandatory objectives, so it's worth exploring the entirety of this open-world section before tackling the bunker, jamming station, and SAM site.

item.title: Student loans voluntary, not compulsory, NELFUND tells tertiary institutions
item.description: … Fund says borrowing is voluntary, urges institutions to stop misleading students By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) has declared that no student in Nigeria’s tertiary institutions is under any obligation to apply for a student loan, insisting that the scheme is designed to assist those facing financial hardship, not compel every student to borrow. The Fund, in a clarification issued on Wednesday, stressed that accessing the interest-free loan remains a personal decision that must be guided by a student’s financial circumstances and genuine need for assistance. NELFUND’s position comes amid the need to ensure that students, tertiary institutions and other stakeholders clearly understand the purpose and conditions of the federal government’s student loan initiative. The Fund explained that the scheme was established to break financial barriers to higher education and prevent eligible Nigerian students from abandoning their academic ambitions because of a lack of funds. It, however, cautioned against any interpretation or practice that could make borrowing compulsory for students, irrespective of their financial capacity. According to the Fund, compelling students who do not need financial assistance to take loans would defeat the very purpose of the programme. “The objective is not to encourage every student to borrow, but to ensure that every eligible Nigerian student who genuinely needs financial assistance has the opportunity to access it,” NELFUND said. It added that the loan scheme was a support mechanism rather than an obligation, stressing that students who could independently meet their educational expenses were free to pursue their studies without applying for the facility. Beyond clarifying the voluntary nature of the scheme, NELFUND reminded prospective beneficiaries that the interest-free facility carries repayment obligations under the provisions of the Student Loans Act. The Fund, therefore, urged students to familiarise themselves with the terms and conditions governing the loans and make informed decisions before submitting applications. While describing the scheme as a critical intervention to expand access to higher education, NELFUND maintained that its priority remained ensuring that financial difficulties did not prevent qualified Nigerian students from pursuing their educational aspirations. The Fund also called on tertiary institutions, student leaders and other stakeholders to provide accurate information about the programme and guide students appropriately, particularly those struggling to finance their education. It reiterated its commitment to ensuring that eligible students who genuinely require financial assistance could access the facility without being misled into believing that taking a loan was a compulsory condition for studying in a Nigerian tertiary institution. The clarification was contained in a statement signed by NELFUND’s Director of Strategic Communications, Mrs Oseyemi Ol

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Mikel Arteta has mastered the art of making substitutions at Arsenal
item.description: Arsenal have beaten Nottingham Forest, Sunderland and Leeds this season thanks to goals from players off the bench By Opta Analyst They say that once is an accident, twice is a coincidence and three times is a pattern. After Mikel Arteta’s substitutes proved decisive yet again for Arsenal, we can say with certainty that his ability to change games from his bench is a pattern worth noting. With Arsenal labouring away at Nottingham Forest and the game drifting towards a goalless draw, Noni Madueke – introduced at half-time – won the game for the visitors , shimmying inside and striking a heavily deflected right-footed shot past Matz Sels. It was hardly a glamorous goal but it secured three valuable Premier League points for Arteta’s side. Continue reading...

item.title: Ebola: Is Nigeria ready?
item.description: T he confirmation of an Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, has renewed concerns about Nigeria’s preparedness for a disease that once threatened to overwhelm parts of the country’s health system. In a statement on Tuesday, Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, confirmed that a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda had tested positive for Ebola after receiving treatment at a private hospital in Abuja. According to the minister, the woman is currently in isolation and receiving medical care. Authorities have identified 44 close contacts and commenced contact tracing to establish whether the patient may have exposed other people to the virus before her diagnosis. APC stifling opposition parties – Makinde Disinflation and household purchasing-power gap Healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and people who may have shared travel links with the patient are among those being investigated as health officials work to contain the infection. The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the FCT Health Services Secretariat and other relevant agencies are coordinating the response. He said, “The Federal Government of Nigeria confirms one case of Ebola disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), following laboratory confirmation today, 20 October 2026. The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received care for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed. She is currently in isolation and receiving medical care. “The FG calls on all public and private healthcare facilities nationwide to be on high alert. Healthcare workers must maintain a high index of suspicion, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases, observe strict infection prevention and control measures, and immediately report suspected cases to public health authorities. “Investigations are ongoing, and we will continue to provide accurate and timely information. We urge Nigerians to remain calm, stay vigilant and cooperate with public health authorities. Early detection, prompt reporting and everyone’s cooperation are critical to preventing further spread. The Government of Nigeria, through the Presidential Taskforce on EVD and NCDC, will continue to provide updates. For information or to report a suspected case, please call NCDC toll-free number 6232.” The development comes against the background of a growing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with related infections reported in Kenya and public health measures activated in Uganda. Nigeria’s Ebola Outbreak Explained Nigeria’s experience with Ebola Nigeria’s experience with Ebola in 2014 demonstrated how quickly an imported infection could become a national public health emergency in a country with a large population and busy international travel routes
item.dc:creator: Daily Trust
item.content:encoded: T he confirmation of an Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Abuja, has renewed concerns about Nigeria’s preparedness for a disease that once threatened to overwhelm parts of the country’s health system. In a statement on Tuesday, Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, confirmed that a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda had tested positive for Ebola after receiving treatment at a private hospital in Abuja. According to the minister, the woman is currently in isolation and receiving medical care. Authorities have identified 44 close contacts and commenced contact tracing to establish whether the patient may have exposed other people to the virus before her diagnosis. APC stifling opposition parties – Makinde Disinflation and household purchasing-power gap Healthcare workers, patients, caregivers and people who may have shared travel links with the patient are among those being investigated as health officials work to contain the infection. The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the FCT Health Services Secretariat and other relevant agencies are coordinating the response. He said, “The Federal Government of Nigeria confirms one case of Ebola disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), following laboratory confirmation today, 20 October 2026. The patient, a woman who recently arrived in Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda, was admitted to a private hospital in the FCT, where she received care for several days before the diagnosis was confirmed. She is currently in isolation and receiving medical care. “The FG calls on all public and private healthcare facilities nationwide to be on high alert. Healthcare workers must maintain a high index of suspicion, promptly identify and isolate suspected cases, observe strict infection prevention and control measures, and immediately report suspected cases to public health authorities. “Investigations are ongoing, and we will continue to provide accurate and timely information. We urge Nigerians to remain calm, stay vigilant and cooperate with public health authorities. Early detection, prompt reporting and everyone’s cooperation are critical to preventing further spread. The Government of Nigeria, through the Presidential Taskforce on EVD and NCDC, will continue to provide updates. For information or to report a suspected case, please call NCDC toll-free number 6232.” The development comes against the background of a growing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), with related infections reported in Kenya and public health measures activated in Uganda. Nigeria’s Ebola Outbreak Explained Nigeria’s experience with Ebola Nigeria’s experience with Ebola in 2014 demonstrated how quickly an imported infection could become a national public health emergency in a country with a large population and busy international travel routes. On July 20, 2014, Patrick Sawyer, a Liberian-American diplomat who was infected with Ebola, arrived at Murtala Muhammed International Airport in Lagos from Liberia. He was subsequently admitted to a private hospital, where his illness was initially difficult to distinguish from other diseases. He died on July 25, 2014. His arrival triggered an emergency response involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Lagos State Government, the NCDC and international health partners. According to a report published in the United States Centres for Disease Control and Prevention’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, Nigeria recorded 20 Ebola cases, comprising 19 laboratory-confirmed cases and one probable case, by September 24, 2014. Eight fatalities from seven laboratory-confirmed Ebola and one probable case were recorded. The deaths included Sawyer and Dr Ameyo Stella Adadevoh, who placed the foreigner in quarantine, as well as six others who were infected during the chain of transmission that followed his arrival. The outbreak was eventually contained, with no new cases reported after August 31, 2014. The country identified and monitored 894 contacts during the response, while 11 patients with laboratory-confirmed Ebola were discharged from care. How prepared is the country for Ebola? Nigeria’s latest preparedness efforts began before the reported FCT case. On June 9, 2026, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu approved the immediate release of N10 billion as emergency intervention funding for public health preparedness and response. The fund is separate from a N21.2 million per-state disbursement under the State Outbreak Investigation and Response Fund. The Presidency also announced the establishment of a Presidential Task Force on Ebola Virus Disease Preparedness and Emerging Public Health Threats, chaired by the Chief of Staff to the President, Femi Gbajabiamila. According to the State House, the fund was intended to strengthen the operational capacity of the NCDC and support critical national public health emergency response activities. The government also directed states hosting international airports and international border corridors, alongside relevant ministries, departments and agencies, to submit their preparedness plans, funding requirements and intervention needs. The measures announced included intensified passenger screening at international airports, enhanced monitoring of passengers arriving through designated high-risk routes, and the activation of referral and isolation centres at the Lagos and Abuja international airports. Other proposed measures included health declaration systems for passengers arriving from or transiting through designated high-risk countries and improved coordination among health, immigration, aviation and security authorities. The funding decision followed warnings about the possibility of Ebola being imported into Nigeria as outbreaks emerged in Central Africa. In a May 28, 2026, advisory, the NCDC assessed Nigeria’s risk of importation as high, citing regional transmission, international travel, population movement, porous land borders and the difficulty of distinguishing early Ebola symptoms from common illnesses such as malaria and Lassa fever. The agency said preparedness needed to cover every state and the FCT, with emphasis on early detection, isolation, laboratory diagnosis, infection prevention and control, contact tracing and the protection of healthcare workers. Daily Trust reported in September that three months later, there was no public breakdown of how the N10 billion was spent, as checks at airports and isolation facilities revealed the presence of the preparedness gap the money was meant to close. Several travellers, who spoke to this paper then, said they were required to provide identification and health information through an app before returning to Nigeria, but to their amazement, no checks were carried out at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, on their arrival. “They didn’t ask me for anything. They didn’t check my provisional sign or QR code, and they didn’t check my temperature. They didn’t do any of that. For me, it was almost a waste of time filling out the form,” one of them, Habeebat Ajayi, had told our correspondent. In a chat with Daily Trust , a medical doctor, Godwin Ekuwke, wondered if designated isolation facilities are fully functional, laboratories can test suspected cases promptly, frontline workers have appropriate protective equipment, and response teams can locate and monitor contacts without delay. He said: “The release of funding is an important step, but its impact depends on timely deployment, transparent expenditure, trained personnel, adequate supplies and coordination between federal and state authorities. “The effectiveness of the response should ultimately be judged by the speed of diagnosis, the quality of care provided, the completeness of contact tracing and the prevention of

item.title: From Sequins to Cow Print, See the Rave Glam Looks at the Tele x Zikora Premiere
item.description: Sophia Chisom, Mike Afolarin, and Genoveva Umeh interpreting the rave glam dress code for Tele x Zikora. A Nollywood premiere is always a good excuse to dress up, but when the dress code says “rave glam,” you know the red carpet is going to be anything but ordinary. That was the scene at the premiere of Tele x Zikora , where the cast and guests stepped out in bold colours, unexpected combinations and outfits that gave us plenty to look at. Written, produced and directed by Adenike Adebayo – Esho , Tele x Zikora is a campus romance set at the fictional Lagos Metropolitan University. The film follows two young people from very different worlds whose paths cross, setting the stage for a love story. Ahead of its cinema release on 23 October 2026, the cast and crew gathered to celebrate, with the evening’s rave glam theme giving everyone room to experiment with their style. Tele x Zikora writer, producer, and director Adenike Adebayo-Esho at the film premiere. Photo Credit: Adenike Adebayo-Esho/Instagram Sophia Chisom gave us a colour combination we wouldn’t have immediately put together, and somehow, it worked. She wore a royal blue longline coat over a matching top with a sharp white collar and cuffs, pairing both with a burnt-orange wrap mini skirt. An orange beret, star drop earrings and white knee-high boots completed her look. Mike Afolarin took a different route with a cow-print shearling jacket, a black top and dark grey flared jeans featuring silver side-buckle details. He finished with a dark cap, keeping things casual while still having a little fun with the dress code. Mike Afolarin at the Tele x Zikora premiere in a cow-print jacket and flare jeans. Photo Credit: Mike Afolarin/Instagram Then there was Genoveva Umeh in magenta and rose-pink sequins. Her dress featured structured shoulders and an asymmetrical skirt with long, shredded ribbons that moved as she walked. She paired it with deep pink tights and metallic heels, making a strong case for wearing pink from head to toe. And those were only a few of the looks from the night. See how the cast and guests dressed for the Tele x Zikora premiere: Genoveva Umeh at the Tele x Zikora premiere in a rose-pink sequined dress and tights. Photo Credit: Genoveva Umeh/Instagram Chimezie Imo at the Tele x Zikora premiere wearing a black tank top, fur coat, and futuristic sunglasses. Photo Credit: Chimezie Imo/Instagram Angel Unigwe attending the Tele x Zikora premiere in a gold metallic top and denim cargo trousers. Photo Credit: Angel Unigwe/Instagram Emeka Nwagbaraocha attending the Tele x Zikora movie premiere in a sleeveless pink shirt and wide-leg trousers. Photo Credit: Emeka Nwagbaraocha/Instagram Gbubemi Ejeye stepping out for the Tele x Zikora premiere in a metallic silver chain dress. Photo Credit: Gbubemi Ejeye/Instagram Eronini Osinachim in a silver metallic jacket and matching trousers for Tele x Zikora. Photo Credit: Eronini Osinachim/Instagram Tomi Ojo in a red leather jacket and pink

item.title: ‘A difficult line’: meet the editors tackling Wikipedia’s arms trade pages
item.description: Volunteers and new recruits come together for ‘wikithon’ to put more detail about industry into public domain “Anyone can edit Wikipedia,” the adage goes. But, it turns out, a relatively small number actually do. What is worthy of a digital page in the world’s largest and most-read encyclopedia is decided by roughly 270,000 active volunteers, enthusiasts who populate the online resource with information on anything from 19th-century medicine to TikTok trends. Inevitably, some subjects are sidelined – the global south, notable women – but a new batch of Wikipedian recruits are waging war on one neglected topic: the arms industry. Last week, in a classroom in central London, two dozen volunteers huddled around laptops and free servings of vegan Ethiopian food for what is known as a “wikithon”, an event of collective and in-person Wikipedia editing. Some were veteran editors in their 70s, others young students who had never registered an account before. But their targets include subjects such as Palantir, Project Maven and Nitro-Chem. Continue reading...

item.title: UK watchdogs urged to tackle suicide social media content after death of girl, 14
item.description: Adriana Retyte took her own life after viewing ‘high-risk’ material on the video-sharing platform TikTok A 14-year-old schoolgirl’s death after TikTok served her suicide content has prompted renewed calls for UK watchdogs to crack down on “toxic” social media feeds. Adriana Retyte, a pupil at Langley school in Norfolk, took her own life after she viewed videos and images related to suicide on the video-sharing platform, according to a coroner who last week found her access to the material on TikTok “may have played a significant part in her decision to take her life”. item.title: Extratropical Cyclone Whips Past Iceland
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Extratropical Cyclone Whips… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search Hurricane Isaias—the only Atlantic hurricane to date in 2026—made landfall in Florida as a Category 2 storm on October 9. After delivering a rainy, windy blow to the U.S. Gulf Coast and drenching much of the Eastern Seaboard, the weather system had more in store. Riding the jet stream east over the North Atlantic, Isaias’s remnants developed into a powerful storm known as an extratropical cyclone . These low-pressure systems often feature asymmetrical, comma-shaped cloud patterns and can strike with hurricane-force winds, rain, and blizzard-like conditions. The VIIRS (Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite) on the NOAA-21 satellite captured this image of the extratropical cyclone brushing past Iceland on the afternoon of October 14. During its journey, the system’s air pressure plummeted by more than 50 hectopascals over a 24-hour period, according to reports —approximately double the criteria for explosive cyclogenesis, or bombogenesis . Some meteorologists believe the storm may have set a new October low for barometric pressure in Iceland, after correcting for altitude, likely breaking a record that has stood since 1963. The cyclone lashed Iceland with high winds as it grazed the coast. A gust of 205 kilometers (128 miles) per hour was recorded near Eyjafjallajökull volcano in the country’s south, while a small island just offshore saw sustained winds of 150 kilometers (93 miles) per hour. Damaging winds extended into northern parts of the country, where residents also braced for sleet and snow. Farther across the Atlantic, northwestern Scotland received gusts up to 90 kilometers (55 miles) per hour on October 14, according to news reports , resulting in cancellations on several ferry routes. NASA Earth Observatory image by Michala Garrison, using VIIRS data from NASA EOSDIS LANCE , GIBS/Worldview , and the Joint Polar Satellite System (JPSS). Story by Lindsey Doermann. item.title: Nervous ISPs replace Chrome as strange consumers of DNS resources
item.description: Google has fixed the flaws in the Chromium browser engine that saw it poll DNS root servers, but ISPs who seem to have odd views about resilience now emerged as a new source of probably-well-meaning overconsumption of internet resources. ICANN’s office of the Chief Technology Officer delivered that view on Monday during the governance org’s annual conference in Bali, Indonesia, in a session that shared recent data from its Identifier Technology Health Indicators (ITHI) research program which monitors the security, stability and resilience of the domain name system. ICANN principal technologist Maud Durand opened with a discussion of “Chromiods” the odd flaw in Chrome that meant well-meaning efforts to avoid a form of DNS hijacking caused the browser to generate about half of all DNS root server traffic during the year 2020. Given Chrome’s enormous prevalence, that traffic was unwelcome. ICANN, plus other internetworking and governance stakeholders, told Google to sort it out. Durand said the Chocolate Factory gradually did. ICANN has kept measuring the impact Chrome makes and Durand shared the graph below which shows the browser’s share of DNS root server traffic falling from 45 percent to one percent today. Or as Durand described it, “in the noise.” ICANN has now detected a new source of odd DNS traffic: ISPs that use multiple DNS servers for every one of their customers’ requests. “Every single DNS query is sent three times: to Google, to Cloudflare, and to another DNS resolver,” Durand said, labelling this practice a “belt and suspenders” approach because a single resolver usually suffices to keep services up. It’s good practice to specify primary and secondary DNS resolvers, in case one doesn’t work. But DNS resolvers are already very resilient, and making multiple requests is unusual. The ISPs ICANN has spotted send DNS requests over IPv4 and IPv6, and for non-cached requests repeat them within 100 milliseconds for about half of queries. A further 30 percent repeat within thirty seconds. “It is hard to know if it is a bug or a specific behaviour,” Durand said, before advancing a personal theory that the ISPs who use this odd resilience technique can’t hire skilled internetworking engineers and therefore created a kind of brute-force resilience routine. The organization is researching the cause. ICANN feels the ISPs using this practice aren’t major players, but the org worries that if the practice becomes widespread, or is adopted by a large entity, it could have a nasty impact. Pointlessly busy DNS servers also matter because ICANN thinks the number of DNS service providers is becoming more concentrated. ICANN has tried to calculate how many DNS resolvers half of internet users can “see” when they are online. As the graph below shows, users could see almost 250 resolver farms in the year 2020. That figure is just under 150 today. Again, Durand isn’t sure why but suspects the number of DNS resolver operators might be shrinking and that the re

item.content:encoded: Google has fixed the flaws in the Chromium browser engine that saw it poll DNS root servers, but ISPs who seem to have odd views about resilience now emerged as a new source of probably-well-meaning overconsumption of internet resources. ICANN principal technologist Maud Durand opened with a discussion of “Chromiods” the odd flaw in Chrome that meant well-meaning efforts to avoid a form of DNS hijacking caused the browser to generate about half of all DNS root server traffic during the year 2020. Given Chrome’s enormous prevalence, that traffic was unwelcome. ICANN, plus other internetworking and governance stakeholders, told Google to sort it out. Durand said the Chocolate Factory gradually did. ICANN has kept measuring the impact Chrome makes and Durand shared the graph below which shows the browser’s share of DNS root server traffic falling from 45 percent to one percent today. Or as Durand described it, “in the noise.” ICANN has now detected a new source of odd DNS traffic: ISPs that use multiple DNS servers for every one of their customers’ requests. “Every single DNS query is sent three times: to Google, to Cloudflare, and to another DNS resolver,” Durand said, labelling this practice a “belt and suspenders” approach because a single resolver usually suffices to keep services up. It’s good practice to specify primary and secondary DNS resolvers, in case one doesn’t work. But DNS resolvers are already very resilient, and making multiple requests is unusual. The ISPs ICANN has spotted send DNS requests over IPv4 and IPv6, and for non-cached requests repeat them within 100 milliseconds for about half of queries. A further 30 percent repeat within thirty seconds. “It is hard to know if it is a bug or a specific behaviour,” Durand said, before advancing a personal theory that the ISPs who use this odd resilience technique can’t hire skilled internetworking engineers and therefore created a kind of brute-force resilience routine. Pointlessly busy DNS servers also matter because ICANN thinks the number of DNS service providers is becoming more concentrated. ICANN has tried to calculate how many DNS resolvers half of internet users can “see” when they are online. As the graph below shows, users could see almost 250 resolver farms in the year 2020. That figure is just under 150 today. Again, Durand isn’t sure why but suspects the number of DNS resolver operators might be shrinking and that the remaining visible resolvers belong to tech giants. ®

item.title: Marvel Officially Made the Saddest Death in MCU History More Tragic With Just 1 Sentence
item.description: In Avengers: Infinity War , when Dr. Strange (Benedict Cumberbatch) and a variety of other heroes are awaiting Thanos’ arrival on Titan, Strange uses the Time Stone to look into alternate futures to see the possible results of the impending conflict. Star Lord (Chris Pratt) asks Strange how many futures he looked into, and Strange replies, “14,000,605.” Then Iron Man (Robert Downey Jr.) asks how many of those resulted in their victory. Strange, looking deep into Stark’s eyes, says, “One.”

item.title: PHP warns it plans to release 2 emergency patches imminently
item.description: Website admins, brace yourselves. Fixes for what are believed to be uncommonly severe vulnerabilities are scheduled to drop in a little more than 12 hours for PHP, a programming language that powers websites and Web applications everywhere. PHP maintainers said Monday that they planned to release patches for two vulnerabilities, both with severity ratings of 9.2 out of a possible 10. Waiting for PHP2Shell “All PHP users are encouraged to prepare now so they can upgrade as soon as the release is available,” the advisory stated. “We reserve the right to release earlier should details of either vulnerability become public, or should evidence of active exploitation appear in the wild.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Red Rising Is Officially Returning In 2027
item.description: In the early 2010s, The Hunger Games captivated a generation, and in its wake came another dystopian tale set in the stars. Red Rising , a six-book saga by author Pierce Brown, traded the death-match arena for Mars, where a rigid, color-coded class system dictates daily life on the Red Planet. "Golds" are the most elite nenbers of Mars society, and they rule over the other colored classes, including the lowest class, "Reds." Much like Katniss Everdeen became the face of a revolution in The Hunger Games , Darrow, a lowborn "Red" miner, becomes the face of Red Rising's revolution.

item.title: Judge dismisses Sam Altman’s sister’s sexual abuse lawsuit

item.title: 1 in 4 cases of depression may be caused by off-kilter body clocks
item.description: Disturbed sleep is a common depression symptom chaiyan Anuwatmongkonchai / Alamy A quarter of depression cases are caused by people’s body clocks being out of whack, a large study suggests. This newly identified “circadian depression” responds poorly to standard antidepressants, but might be eased by taking melatonin or adopting behavioural strategies, like going outside in the early morning sun. “The coordination of [your body clocks] underpins your mood, your metabolism, your concentration, your sleep-wake cycle and many other key factors,” says Ian Hickie at the University of Sydney. “When it’s well, you feel really well, you get up in the morning full of energy. When it’s off, you feel jet-lagged all the time, you feel tired, you feel exhausted, you gain weight, you can’t concentrate, you sleep poorly and your behaviour changes.” Read more How to harness your body clock for a longer, healthier life Hickie and his colleagues asked more than 10,000 people in Australia with severe, recurrent depression to fill out surveys about their sleep patterns and other characteristics, such as whether their symptoms change seasonally. The participants also provided saliva samples for DNA analysis. Advertisement Of these participants, 23 per cent were identified as having circadian depression. This meant they exhibited at least three of six signs of body clock dysregulation: being an “evening type”, going to sleep later than most people, feeling very tired when getting up regardless of sleep duration, sleeping more during bouts of depression, sleeping in late on non-work days, and experiencing strong seasonal changes in mood, energy, sleep and appetite. “It’s not only about the quantity or the amount of sleep, it’s really about the rhythm and the regularity of sleep,” says team member Emiliana Tonini , also at the University of Sydney. Those with circadian depression tended to have more severe symptoms than those with non-circadian depression, including more suicidal thoughts. They also developed symptoms at an earlier age – the average age of onset was 18 in the circadian-depression group and 23 in the non-circadian group. item.dc:creator: Alice Klein
item.content:encoded: Disturbed sleep is a common depression symptom chaiyan Anuwatmongkonchai / Alamy A quarter of depression cases are caused by people’s body clocks being out of whack, a large study suggests. This newly identified “circadian depression” responds poorly to standard antidepressants, but might be eased by taking melatonin or adopting behavioural strategies, like going outside in the early morning sun. “The coordination of [your body clocks] underpins your mood, your metabolism, your concentration, your sleep-wake cycle and many other key factors,” says Ian Hickie at the University of Sydney. “When it’s well, you feel really well, you get up in the morning full of energy. When it’s off, you feel jet-lagged all the time, you feel tired, you feel exhausted, you gain weight, you can’t concentrate, you sleep poorly and your behaviour changes.” Read more How to harness your body clock for a longer, healthier life Hickie and his colleagues asked more than 10,000 people in Australia with severe, recurrent depression to fill out surveys about their sleep patterns and other characteristics, such as whether their symptoms change seasonally. The participants also provided saliva samples for DNA analysis. Advertisement Of these participants, 23 per cent were identified as having circadian depression. This meant they exhibited at least three of six signs of body clock dysregulation: being an “evening type”, going to sleep later than most people, feeling very tired when getting up regardless of sleep duration, sleeping more during bouts of depression, sleeping in late on non-work days, and experiencing strong seasonal changes in mood, energy, sleep and appetite. “It’s not only about the quantity or the amount of sleep, it’s really about the rhythm and the regularity of sleep,” says team member Emiliana Tonini , also at the University of Sydney. Those with circadian depression tended to have more severe symptoms than those with non-circadian depression, including more suicidal thoughts. They also developed symptoms at an earlier age – the average age of onset was 18 in the circadian-depression group and 23 in the non-circadian group. Free newsletter Sign up to Health Check Sign up to newsletter Body clock dysregulation and the resulting mood disturbances may be caused by genetic factors, the study found. The participants with circadian depression were more likely to have genetic variants linked to sleep problems, higher body weight, inflammatory markers and ADHD. “There is an underlying biology that is quite distinct from other forms of depression,” says Tonini. Another contributing factor may be our modern lifestyles, says Hickie. Our body clocks need to be reset each morning by light exposure to maintain steady, 24-hour rhythms and can be destabilised by artificial light exposure at times when we would have historically been in the dark, he says. “We live in the 21 st century, which says, you know, ‘Stay inside, be on a computer all day, avoid the light and then stay up at night and expose yourself to light’”. This is “a complete reverse of what we’re built for”. The participants identified as having circadian depression reported less efficacy and more side effects when they took common antidepressants like selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors. This may be because these SSRIs target a form of depression related to the neurotransmitter serotonin. Let a breakthrough in measuring body clocks ease the ills of shiftwork New tests to gauge an individual’s circadian rhythms could be put to good use helping night workers fend off the ill effects of their unsocial hours The researchers are about to launch a clinical trial to investigate whether taking a synthetic form of the hormone melatonin, which regulates sleep-wake cycles, might be more effective for treating circadian depression. They previously found that an antidepressant called agomelatine, which mimics melatonin’s effects in the brain, improved sleep and reduced general depression . The trial will also explore whether behavioural strategies for body clock regulation reduce depression. These include waking up at the same time every morning around sunrise and going outside, spending time outside again in the middle of the day when the sun is brightest, and having regular mealtimes and exercise times during daylight hours. Once it gets dark, Hickie recommends not eating large meals, exercising or being exposed to bright lights. “They are all the wrong signals,” he says. Aside from helping with depression, rejigging body clocks may also reduce inflammation and promote healthy weight, says Hickie. He hopes that, in the future, early identification of circadian depression will allow people to be treated more effectively and spare them from taking medications that are inappropriate for them. “If you get on the right track first off, you’re more likely to get out of the hole you’re in and more likely to have better longer-term mental health, but also physical health,” he says. How bad is modern life for our body clocks – and what can we do? Modern life disrupts the circadian rhythms controlling our biology – increasing our risk of developing conditions ranging from diabetes to dementia. Lynne Peeples’s new book The Inner Clock explores and offers solutions The findings are “really useful because they advance the field in terms of understanding the whole circadian rhythm aspect of depression and how it might be related to biological measures like genetics and inflammatory markers”, says Colleen Loo at the University of New South Wales in Sydney. However, more research is needed before circadian depression can be formally recognised as a new subtype of depression, says Loo. “As a clinical psychiatrist, I don’t think it’s time for us to say, ‘Right, based on this, we’re going to say that, if you have these symptoms, we should treat you with this medication rather than that medication,’” she says. Nevertheless, people with depression could consider trying melatonin and behavioural strategies in addition to their current treatments if they believe their body clocks aren’t functioning optimally, says Loo. Melatonin is available only on prescription in the UK and Australia, but not in the US. “Melatonin is a safe medication and things like low lighting before bed is sensible anyway,” says Loo. “All clinicians should be talking to patients about these things if they have sleep disturbances.” Journal Reference: British Journal of Psychiatry DOI: 10.1192/bjp.2026.10798 Need a listening ear? item.title: Indian certification authority eMudhra’s private keys compromised – one of them was the number ‘4’
item.description: Tragically simple private keys used by a certification authority based in India have been compromised, meaning the 60-million-plus certs it has issued can’t be trusted and necessitating a massive clean-up job. The CA of concern in this case is called eMudhra, which boasts of having issued over 60 million digital certificates to help usher in a world of digital trust. The company has instead panicked the world. News of the company’s errors appeared on Tuesday in a post by Dennis Jackson, a member of Mozilla’s cryptography engineering team. “On Saturday, October 17, at 20:06 UTC, Mozilla received a report from a community member that private keys associated with eight eMudhra intermediate certificates had been compromised,” he wrote . “These keys could allow attackers to issue fraudulent HTTPS certificates for websites they do not control.” Or as Cloudflare put it , “an attacker can create a forged certificate for any domain and use it to impersonate servers to intercept or modify traffic.” Jackson has since elaborated on the incident and the response, which has thankfully seen Mozilla, Chrome, and Apple remediate the issue so their browsers won’t rely on the certificates – at least after users install an update. He also reports that eMudhra has revoked the certs, and lists many FOSS projects that have issued updates that mean they won’t recognize certs from eMudhra. That’s welcome, but sadly certs signed with these private keys are still out there and many services rely on them. Browser makers are set up to detect and reject bad certs. Others who relied on them may not be, and will likely need to dig into their environments to see if they rely on certs signed by eMudhra. Developer Geoffrey Huntley has offered some advice on automating that process. At the time of writing, eMudhra has not responded to The Register ’s inquiries about the incident and its security practices. The latter question is of great interest because security researcher Scott Helme analyzed eMudhra’s certs and found one the private keys it used “is the number 4.” “Not a number that starts with 4, or the number 4 followed by a few hundred random digits, just, 4... Another one is 56, and another is 115. I know, because I recovered all of them from their public certificates on my laptop just now, and it took less than a second,” Helme wrote. Other researchers have found private keys including the numbers 66, 155, 156, 230 and 237. Those are vastly inadequate keys, because they’re easy to guess, making all certs issued by eMudhra susceptible to brute force attacks. As Helme put it: “A P-384 private key should be a random 384-bit number, which gives you 2³⁸⁴ possibilities (or roughly 10¹¹⁵), so nobody is ever going to search that.” This is a developing story and The Register will update it as more information becomes available. ®

item.title: Meet Solange Omon, the 21-Year-Old Cameroonian Model Who Made Her Victoria’s Secret Runway Debut
item.description: Solange Omon walking the runway in illuminated wings and a sweeping metallic train at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. Photo Credit: Solange Omon/Instagram Did you see an African woman on the runway of the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show? She walked with such a composed, smooth step that you couldn’t help but notice her as she stepped out into the bright spotlights of Los Angeles. Her name is Solange Omon , a 21-year-old rising star who has officially earned her wings as the newest Victoria’s Secret Angel. She secured her place on the global stage after beating over 100,000 applicants in the brand’s open casting search, Angels Among Us. The competition, documented in a special YouTube series, crowned her as the winner, awarding her a one-year modelling contract with IMG Models alongside her runway debut. Solange Omon with fellow Angels Among Us top 3 finalists Andreína Martínez and Tatyana Tinsley. Photo Credit: Solange Omon/Instagram Born in Cameroon as the eldest of six children, Solange moved to the United States and has spent the last few years living in Lewiston, Maine. Before entering the national spotlight, her everyday life looked quite different. She spent her time balancing university coursework with her job as a programme coordinator for a local non-profit organisation focused on supporting young people. Her work centred on helping Black and immigrant teenagers apply for jobs, find professional mentors, and access higher education resources across her community. When she attended the open casting call in Chicago, she carried that grounded background straight onto the runway. For her big moment, she wore a contrast ivory and black lace lingerie set featuring a plunge bra paired with high-cut briefs, styled with oversized gold hoop drop earrings . The focus of her outfit was a pair of illuminated golden wings featuring embedded warm lights, paired with a sweeping bronze metallic train attached at the base of the wings . Solange Omon walking the runway in illuminated wings and a sweeping metallic train at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. Photo Credit: Solange Omon/Instagram As she walked down the glossy black runway, she held the edges of her metallic train, letting the lightweight fabric float behind her as she moved . Midway through her walk, she turned toward the cameras with a warm smile, twirled gracefully on the catwalk, and gestured to the audience before stepping back up the stage . Her milestone victory marks a significant moment for African representation in global fashion, showing how a young woman from Central Africa went from community work to one of the most recognised runways in the world. Solange Omon backstage at the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show in Los Angeles after earning her Angel wings. Photo Credit: Solange Omon/Instagram The post Meet Solange Omon, the 21-Year-Old Cameroonian Model Who Made Her Victoria’s Secret Runway Debut appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!

item.title: SpaceX will attempt 1st-ever double Starship rocket catch on next test launch, a 'profound technology milestone,' Elon Musk says
item.description: null SpaceX will soon notch a huge spaceflight milestone, if all goes according to plan. The company will try to catch both stages of its Starship megarocket during the vehicle's next test flight, which is targeted for next month, founder and CEO Elon Musk announced during SpaceX's quarter 3 (Q3) earnings call today (Oct. 20). If SpaceX succeeds, this "will be the first time that an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered," Musk said. "The only way that we can extend consciousness beyond Earth on a sustained basis is with a fully reusable orbital launch vehicle. So this is, I think, a profound technology milestone in the history of civilization and consciousness." Artist's illustration of SpaceX catching the upper stage of its Starship megarocket, something the company expects to do on the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing more than 400 feet (122 meters) tall when fully stacked. As Musk noted, both of its stages — the Super Heavy booster and Ship spacecraft — are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable, a breakthrough that SpaceX thinks will make Mars settlement and other grand exploration feats economically feasible. Starship's recovery strategy is different than that for SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets, which are partially reusable. (The latter two rockets have expendable upper stages). Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy boosters come back to Earth on landing pads near the launch site or on ships at sea downrange. Super Heavy and Ship, however, will steer themselves directly back to their launch tower, which will capture each vehicle with its "chopstick" arms. This will allow SpaceX to inspect, refurbish and refly Starship at an accelerated rate, which is a priority for the company: Musk has said he envisions launching Starship more than 10,000 times per year by 2030. Starship has conducted 14 test flights to date, and SpaceX has pulled off chopstick catches with Super Heavy on three of them. The company has not yet tried to catch Ship, which is a more difficult proposition, as the upper stage travels higher, farther and faster than the booster does. Still, Musk is confident that SpaceX will pull off a Ship catch on the first try. (He did not give a specific target date for Flight 15, saying only that it was expected next month.) "I'd say it's more likely than not that this succeeds next flight," he said. "And if not, we have a steady stream of Starship flight attempts through the end of this year, and and then accelerating next year." Success would mean back-to-back Starship flights with huge milestones. On Flight 14, which occurred on Sept. 28, Ship reached orbit for the first time ever . It also deployed 26 of SpaceX's Starlink Version 3 satellites — the first 26 members of a next-gen broadband constellation in low Earth orbit that will eventually consist of about 100,000 spacecraft . item.dc:creator: Mike Wall
item.content:encoded: null SpaceX will soon notch a huge spaceflight milestone, if all goes according to plan. The company will try to catch both stages of its Starship megarocket during the vehicle's next test flight, which is targeted for next month, founder and CEO Elon Musk announced during SpaceX's quarter 3 (Q3) earnings call today (Oct. 20). If SpaceX succeeds, this "will be the first time that an orbital launch vehicle has been fully recovered," Musk said. "The only way that we can extend consciousness beyond Earth on a sustained basis is with a fully reusable orbital launch vehicle. So this is, I think, a profound technology milestone in the history of civilization and consciousness." Artist's illustration of SpaceX catching the upper stage of its Starship megarocket, something the company expects to do on the vehicle's 15th test flight. (Image credit: SpaceX) Starship is the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, standing more than 400 feet (122 meters) tall when fully stacked. As Musk noted, both of its stages — the Super Heavy booster and Ship spacecraft — are designed to be fully and rapidly reusable, a breakthrough that SpaceX thinks will make Mars settlement and other grand exploration feats economically feasible. Starship's recovery strategy is different than that for SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets, which are partially reusable. (The latter two rockets have expendable upper stages). Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy boosters come back to Earth on landing pads near the launch site or on ships at sea downrange. Super Heavy and Ship, however, will steer themselves directly back to their launch tower, which will capture each vehicle with its "chopstick" arms. This will allow SpaceX to inspect, refurbish and refly Starship at an accelerated rate, which is a priority for the company: Musk has said he envisions launching Starship more than 10,000 times per year by 2030. Starship has conducted 14 test flights to date, and SpaceX has pulled off chopstick catches with Super Heavy on three of them. The company has not yet tried to catch Ship, which is a more difficult proposition, as the upper stage travels higher, farther and faster than the booster does. Still, Musk is confident that SpaceX will pull off a Ship catch on the first try. (He did not give a specific target date for Flight 15, saying only that it was expected next month.) "I'd say it's more likely than not that this succeeds next flight," he said. "And if not, we have a steady stream of Starship flight attempts through the end of this year, and and then accelerating next year." Success would mean back-to-back Starship flights with huge milestones. On Flight 14, which occurred on Sept. 28, Ship reached orbit for the first time ever . It also deployed 26 of SpaceX's Starlink Version 3 satellites — the first 26 members of a next-gen broadband constellation in low Earth orbit that will eventually consist of about 100,000 spacecraft . The Starship Flight 15 preview was something of an aside during today's call. The event primarily served to announce SpaceX's financial performance during Q3, the three-month stretch that ended on Sept. 30. And that performance was strong, company representatives said. SpaceX recorded revenues of $14.6 billion during Q3, an increase of 161% from the $5.6 billion earned during Q3 of 2025. The company had a net income of $4.4 billion during Q3, $5.5 billion better than the result from the same stretch last year, when SpaceX lost $1.1 billion. Just $1.8 billion of 2026 Q3 revenue came from SpaceX's launch division. The vast majority was generated by two other segments — connectivity (services provided by its Starlink megaconstellation) and artificial intelligence (or, as the Trump administration has recently rebranded it, "superintelligence"). SpaceX thinks these latter two segments will continue to boom. That's why it's building the infrastructure to support thousands of Starship launches per year — to loft lots of Starlink satellites and AI data centers to Earth orbit. And the company believes that it's positioned to really start raking in the cash, starting as soon as next year. "In a nutshell, what this implies for SpaceX annual recurring revenue by the end of '27 is somewhere between 500 billion [dollars] and a trillion," Musk said.

item.title: Trump is giving Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million fraud bounty program
item.description: Influencer Nick Shirley listens as US President Donald Trump makes an announcement on fraud in the Oval Office of the White House in Washington, DC, on October 20, 2026. (Photo by Jim WATSON / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance said on Tuesday that the Trump administration was giving right-wing YouTuber Nick Shirley $10,000 and launching a $25 million bounty program for members of the public to report fraud. In December 2025, Shirley published a viral video alleging fraud at daycares in Minnesota that were operated by members of the local Somali community. Shirley lingered in parking lots and asked to enter childcare centers, taking refusals as evidence that the centers weren't actually caring for children. The video quickly went viral, triggering a massive governmental response: Federal immigration agents descended on the … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Merging SpaceX and Tesla would be a "good idea," Musk says
item.description: Elon Musk said Tuesday that he would like to see the consolidation of his business empire by formally merging his two largest companies, SpaceX and Tesla. "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said of a potential merger. He was speaking during a question-and-answer period as part of SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call. Musk said, ultimately, it not his decision. "But at the end of the day the shareholders have to be supportive of this." Musk's talk of a merger comes after a busy year in which SpaceX already acquired Musk's artificial intelligence firm, xAI, in February. In June, SpaceX went public with the largest initial public offering on record. Read full article Comments

item.title: Auto tech startup claims it traced hack attempt back to rival's IP address
item.description: An automotive tech startup claims that its IT systems were attacked by individuals trying to steal its driving model, and that those attacks came from an IP address associated with a rival in the space. The tech startup, IQ.Lvbs, described the alleged security incident in a recent blog post . On October 3, IQ.Lvbs introduced the private beta of NovaSpark , the first model for the company's IQ.Pilot app, in the Comma.ai Discord channel. They put it in that channel because the model requires the use of Comma.ai's camera hardware, which is built for self-driving vehicles. From there, things got weird. "From October 7 to 14, we faced repeated attempts to steal NovaSpark, access users’ devices and private driving files, and exploit our sign-in system," the IQ.Lvbs blog post claims. "The first requests came from an IP assigned to Comma.ai Inc." In addition, on October 8 – shortly after the alleged attacks began – somebody banned IQ.Lvbs' team from the Comma.ai Discord channel. Posts on the IQ.Pilot Discord channel indicate that individuals doing private beta testing for IQ.Lvbs have also been banned from that channel. One of the three people involved in IQ.Lvbs, a UI/UX designer who asked to be identified only as "Cat," speculated to The Register about the reasons for the alleged hack and Discord ban. "Our model, NovaSpark, is a good deal ahead of Comma's latest small and large models, which directly threatens their core business of making AI models good enough to sell their hardware," he said. "Comma for the most part has been stagnant in their models' improvement and that was a main driver for us making NovaSpark." An October 7, 2026 Discord message from user Torq_boi, said to be Harald Schäfer, Comma.ai’s CTO, implies NovaSpark was distilled from Comma.ai's Rebellious Hope model. “I’m glad people are training models and experimenting with this stuff," the post starts. "But don’t lie to people about what you’re doing, and saying it’s not a finetune of existing comma models when it is. That’s not cool.” IQ.Lvbs disputes that assertion and says it did the work on its own. "The claim that NovaSpark is Rebellious Hope with a short fine-tune and an unchanged policy does not survive scrutiny, and we’re not sure how Comma came to that conclusion, especially considering that they do not possess NovaSpark’s model weights or ONNX," the biz said. In the log data IQ.Lvbs published to support its claims, the company flags the username haraschax as one of those associated with Comma.ai IP addresses. Schäfer uses that username on GitHub. Comma.ai and Schäfer did not respond to requests for comment sent to several different addresses. The Discord user Torq_boi in the Comma.ai channel did not respond to a DM seeking comment. Comma.ai is currently being investigated [PDF] by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to assess whether its driving automation tech contributed to five crashes and three deaths. item.title: Cops raid office of RFK Jr. allies planning “unethical” vaccine trial on babies
item.description: Police in Guinea-Bissau raided the offices of Danish researchers on Monday, seizing doses of hepatitis B vaccine intended for a vaccine trial for newborns. International health experts have called the trial " unethical ," but anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has attempted to fund it with US taxpayer dollars. Under Kennedy, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention announced in December that it had awarded the Danish researchers—led by married couple Peter Aaby and Christine Stabell Benn of Bandim Health Project— an unsolicited $1.6 million grant to run the trial . Aaby and Stabell Benn are controversial vaccine researchers who claim vaccines cause overlooked harms. They have been repeatedly praised by Kennedy, but are currently under investigation for alleged scientific misconduct by Danish authorities. Plans for the trial were halted in January as widespread condemnation erupted over the trial's design, which would potentially expose thousands of newborns in the country to hepatitis B, risking a lifelong infection that can lead to liver cirrhosis, cancer, and premature death. Outrage flared again after a Rolling Stone story earlier this month claimed the CDC set aside another $1.6 million in funding in late September and planned to move forward with the trial. Read full article Comments

item.title: Tesla and SpaceX are discussing a possible merger, Musk says
item.description: Tesla and SpaceX have formed special committees to discuss a possible merger, Elon Musk said during the latter's third quarter earnings call Tuesday . Musk, who serves as CEO of both companies, said the special committees were formed at the request of shareholders and consist of independent directors (though he did not name them). He also noted that he is not a member of either committee, nor involved in any of the discussions. "Because I'm a conflicted party, I can't actually be in the discussions of the special committees," Musk said. "So it's an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking and I can't be in the conversation. … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Microsoft reportedly projects $1,200 to $1,800 price for 2028 Project Helix
item.description: We haven't heard many details about Microsoft's upcoming "Project Helix" gaming hardware since the company announced it in March as a device that will "play your Xbox and PC games." In a new wide-ranging profile of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma , though, Fortune alludes to a dual release strategy for upcoming Microsoft gaming hardware, with "a next-generation handheld device" planned by the end of next year and a 2028 holiday season console release that could cost between $1,200 and $1,800. That future console price range is based on what has "internally been projected" at the company, according to Fortune. But the price for consumers could come down if "Microsoft decides to subsidize the cost," the outlet says, as many console makers have done in the past . While a $1,200 starting price would be historically high for the game console market, even accounting for inflation , it also reflects a new normal: The slowdown in Moore's Law and AI-driven component shortages mean cutting-edge gaming hardware just isn't as cheap as it used to be. This year, the Steam Machine broke the $1,000 starting price , while the 2-year-old technology in the PlayStation 5 Pro is now going for $900 , and the 6-year-old Xbox Series X now starts at $750 . Read full article Comments

item.title: Mac Allister double sparks Liverpool’s thrilling comeback win over Villarreal
item.description: Andoni Iraola and Iñigo Pérez parked a long and close friendship in the buildup to their first competitive confrontation as coaches. The old Athletic Bilbao teammates will have a humdinger of a Champions League contest to dissect once communications are restored. Liverpool, ignited by Rio Ngumoha, recovered from two goals down against Villarreal to maintain their 100% record plus their gathering momentum. Alexis Mac Allister struck twice, Florian Wirtz capped recent improvement with his first goal of the season while Liverpool were dreadful for the opening 30 minutes, transformed after the break and fretting in stoppage time after Tani Oluwaseyi had volleyed in a third for Villarreal. The game flipped on Sergi Cardona’s mistake and Ronald Araújo’s equaliser with the final touch of the first half. “We weren’t able to handle the emotion tonight,” conceded Villarreal coach Pérez. Continue reading...
